This is a Systems engineer expert draft for the lifecycle rehearsal, not an approved specification. It responds to the domain draft at sequence 4, the Human-centered designer draft at sequence 6 and the Understand synthesis at sequence 8. These events supply proposed requirements, not participant evidence. The seed supplies A/B/C and the operating constraints. No technical checks, human approval or field results exist.

Problem framing and rival explanations — D1.problem

The task is to help learners represent what fictional garden records support. A reasoning deficit has not been established. Apparent difficulty could instead arise from inaccessible wording, unfamiliar story units, navigation, time pressure, unequal device control or reluctance to disagree with an adult. A learner may understand the uncertainty and reject the framing. Training learners to comply with the interface would not resolve these explanations.

The principal systems challenge is maintaining a faithful, revisable record while people share one device. Interaction authority and representational authority differ: operating a control does not establish permission to speak for others. The tool cannot authenticate agreement without introducing personal records or unsupported inferences. It should expose attribution choices and leave disputed agreement to human facilitation.

Requirement S1: visible, contestable representation

Origin: Systems engineer, extending sequences 4, 6 and 8. The final record must show a learner-selected representation status: one offered explanation, agreed group explanation or unresolved discussion. Default to one offered explanation; never infer agreement from completion, silence or passing. Provide a disagreement marker independent of claim revision. A disagreement marker combined with an agreement label must produce a neutral request to review the representation, not silently alter either selection. The group can choose unresolved discussion without adding text.

Human reason: learners need a practical way to contest attribution; a facilitator needs a way to pause recording without deciding whose science explanation wins. System reason: the application can faithfully display selections but cannot verify consent or consensus.

Observable acceptance check: a reviewer selects agreement, then marks disagreement; both remain visible until deliberately corrected, and the summary identifies the representation as needing review. Passing preserves existing contributions. No output states that all learners agreed as an independently verified fact.

Support dependency: credible dissent depends on adult conduct, group norms, language support and time. Student review of whether refusal feels possible remains pending. The product must not claim that a disagreement control establishes belonging or psychological safety.

Requirement S2: separately authored planning fixtures

Origin: Systems engineer, resolving a source-data dependency identified in sequences 4, 6 and 8. The following are proposed additional invented records for review. They are newly authored rehearsal fixtures, not supplied observations, measurements or extensions of A/B/C. Original starting height, plant type and soil remain unrecorded.

Fixture W — hold recorded light constant; compare recorded water.
W1: invented 14-day story; starting height 4 cm; fictional plant type T; fictional soil mix S; water 1 story unit/day; bright light; final height 11 cm; upright leaves.
W2: invented 14-day story; starting height 4 cm; fictional plant type T; fictional soil mix S; water 2 story units/day; bright light; final height 13 cm; upright leaves.
Descriptive output: recorded water differs; recorded light, starting height, type, soil and duration match. W2 finishes 2 cm taller in this prepared story. Temperature, individual variation and other conditions are unrecorded; replication and allocation method are unspecified. This difference does not establish what caused the outcome.

Fixture L — hold recorded water constant; compare recorded light.
L1: invented 14-day story; starting height 4 cm; fictional plant type T; fictional soil mix S; water 2 story units/day; bright light; final height 9 cm; upright leaves.
L2: invented 14-day story; starting height 4 cm; fictional plant type T; fictional soil mix S; water 2 story units/day; dim light; final height 14 cm; drooping leaves.
Descriptive output: recorded light differs; recorded water, starting height, type, soil and duration match. L2 finishes 5 cm taller in this prepared story. Temperature, individual variation and other conditions are unrecorded; replication and allocation method are unspecified. Leaf appearance does not validate health, and this difference does not establish causation.

Interaction mapping: offer two supported choices, “Hold light constant; compare water” and “Hold water constant; compare light.” The first selects W1/W2; the second selects L1/L2. Display the matching recorded conditions alongside the selected comparison. Do not imply that the learner has actually controlled conditions or conducted an experiment. If a learner wants to hold additional unrecorded conditions constant, a facilitation prompt can preserve that proposal; the application must not fabricate another example or calculated outcome.

Human reason: the learner can connect a planning choice to a visible comparison while questioning its limits. System reason: a fixed lookup is inspectable and avoids an unsupported plant-growth model.

Observable acceptance check: switching W to L changes card identifiers, exact records, graphics and difference text together; switching back restores W exactly. No unsupported control combination produces an outcome. Both fixtures retain invented-data labels and unknowns. A/B/C remain exactly as supplied, with their missing fields unchanged.

These fixtures are a reviewable proposal, not settled source authority. Domain and teacher review must examine whether their final-height differences inadvertently cue a preferred explanation. Rejection or replacement of the fixtures remains possible before Design.

Requirement S3: transactional editing and bounded recovery — D4.verification

Origin: Systems engineer, specifying the recovery requirement in sequences 4, 6 and 8. Distinguish the initial committed claim and pair, the later committed position and pair, and a pending edit. Use at most two optional text entries on the main path: initial own wording and later own wording. Evidence selection, representation and dissent use named controls. Selecting retain, narrow, revise or withhold must not silently rewrite either text entry.

An edit opens a pending proposal showing current and proposed content. Confirm commits exactly the reviewed proposal. Cancel discards the proposal and preserves the current record. An explicit correction to the initial record must identify the corrected version and keep the original visible within the current activity; it must not rewrite history as if the corrected text had always been entered.

Provide one clearly labeled within-group recovery snapshot of the state preceding the latest committed change. It includes claims, pairs, reconsideration action, reveal state, planning choice, representation, dissent and optional practice state. Preview the snapshot before restoring it; cancellation leaves the current state untouched. A successful restore consumes that snapshot, so the control does not promise an unlimited history. Draft keystrokes are not separate recovery entries.

Human reason: users need to repair accidental edits without losing authorship. System reason: explicit state boundaries prevent cancel, correction and recovery from having ambiguous effects.

Observable acceptance check: enter distinctive fictional wording, change the evidence pair, cancel an edit and inspect unchanged committed content. Commit a different proposal, preview recovery, cancel recovery, then restore it. Confirm that wording and all associated selections return together. Correct the initial record and verify that original and correction are distinguishable. No check has been performed.

Requirement S4: shared-device handoff clears every activity layer

Origin: Systems engineer, extending the seed and sequences 4, 6 and 8. Handoff requires a compact confirmation. Cancel preserves the entire activity. Confirm clears committed records, pending drafts, original/corrected versions, selections, representation, dissent, reveal progress, planning choice, optional practice and recovery. Clear application-owned input values, displayed summaries, announcements and retained state references. Only public fictional fixtures and an empty opening state remain.

The reset must work from an unfinished edit, a recovery preview and optional practice. Recovery cannot cross a confirmed handoff. No storage, telemetry or network is permitted; state is held only for the current in-memory activity. Reopening starts empty.

Human reason: the next group should not inherit the previous group’s wording or disputes. System reason: clearing only visible fields leaves hidden drafts and recovery available.

Observable acceptance check: populate every layer with distinctive fictional marker text, cancel handoff and verify preservation. Confirm handoff and inspect application controls, summaries, announcements, drafts and recovery for absence of the markers; recovery remains unavailable. Repeat from a pending edit and optional practice. These are proposed technical checks, not privacy certification or completed results.

Brief help must explain that clearing the activity does not control screenshots, browser history, autofill, operating-system features or other device records. Ordinary browser limits should not displace the learner mission.

Requirement S5: access and facilitation are coupled dependencies — D1.coupling

Origin: Systems engineer, operationalizing sequences 4, 6 and 8. All decisions must be keyboard operable with named controls, visible focus and readable selection states. Evidence graphics need consistent final-height scales, numeric centimetre labels and text equivalents. C must appear through an explicit reveal action with an accessible notification and predictable focus. Planning changes must announce which prepared comparison is displayed without moving the user away from the control.

Human requirements: available facilitation for discussion and disputed attribution; workable oral, scribed or multilingual contributions; permission to pass; sufficient time and materials. Teachers need flexible device turns that do not turn rotation into a participation test. These conditions are unknown, not assumed resources.

System requirements: low entry burden, no required typing, at most two main-path text entries, visible unknowns, equal-status reconsideration routes and a complete paper package. The paper package must contain the mission, exact A/B records, separately revealed C, labeled comparison visuals with text equivalents, both proposed fixtures and their choice instructions, and an initial/later claim-and-evidence record with representation and dissent choices.

Observable acceptance check: a reviewer completes the decisions by keyboard, can interpret every comparison using text alone and retains access at narrow width and enlarged text. A teacher reviewer can conduct the same sequence from paper alone without consulting browser controls. No accessibility, paper-equivalence or workload checks have occurred.

Non-training levers include simplifying instructions, choosing paper-only delivery, providing a scribe or translation support, adjusting lesson scope, changing device-turn arrangements and pausing disputed attribution. If these supports are unavailable, reduce scope or reject the browser activity rather than attribute difficulty to learner capability.

Authority, dissent and review gates

Learners retain authority over their wording and attribution requests. A facilitator supports discussion and correction; the interface must not assign them authority to infer agreement or grade reasoning. Proposed reviewers include science practitioners for framing and fixture consistency, teachers and support staff for workload and materials, students for access and credible dissent, and caregivers for representation and shared-device expectations. These are proposed responsibilities, not accepted assignments or approvals.

Retain the objections from sequences 4 and 6: C may feel like a trap, suggested claims may constrain interpretation, and a polished group record may conceal disagreement. This draft adds explicit attribution conflict handling, a source-separated fixture proposal and bounded recovery. No scenario event was supplied, so these changes respond to draft dependencies rather than an observed incident.

The system supports descriptive comparison and faithful representation. Coupled requirements and acceptance checks

R1 — Focused entry and inspectable comparison. Origin: domain, sequence 4; Human-centered designer, sequence 6; Understand synthesis, sequence 8. Open with a short mission to help the fictional garden team explain what its records support. Begin with A/B, a claim choice and pair selection. Suggested claims may include a bounded observation, a broader claim to investigate and a statement of causal uncertainty; own wording and withholding remain available without a preferred-answer hierarchy. With only A/B revealed, A/B is the sole available pair: present its selection honestly as confirming the initial comparison. After C, pair selection becomes a choice among A/B, A/C and B/C.

Reason: entry should depend on an intelligible decision, not writing stamina or an appearance of choice. Evidence graphics use a consistent final-height scale with centimetre values and full text equivalents. Show water, light, leaf appearance, fictional status and unknowns in words.

Acceptance check: a reviewer can choose or withhold a claim and confirm A/B without typing, then choose every available pair after C. Values and difference descriptions match the source specification. Graphics do not rename final height as growth or leaves as health. These checks are planned, not performed.

Descriptive feedback reports records and differences; it does not judge whether the selected pair proves the claim.

Reason: reconsideration must remain an opportunity to examine scope, not obedience to a hidden answer. An action selection must never silently rewrite wording. Reason: system interaction authority is narrower than authority to represent people. A compact shared record needs explicit limits and a human route for disputed attribution.

Acceptance check: select agreement, mark disagreement and inspect the conflict notice; deliberately choose unresolved discussion and verify the correction. Passing preserves existing work. Dependencies, support and stopping conditions

Target languages, reading supports, devices, browsers, lesson duration, staffing, printing and preparation responsibility remain unknown. Design can specify a candidate under explicit assumptions; it cannot claim those conditions exist. Before any pilot, proposed responsible humans must establish feasible support and workload, review the materials and decide whether disputed attribution has a credible resolution process.

If support is unavailable, reduce scope, alter facilitation, choose paper-only delivery or reject the candidate rather than infer learner incapability. Do not treat flexible roles, a disagreement control or an attractive interface as evidence of belonging or equitable participation.

Tradeoffs and retained dissent

Suggested claims lower entry burden but can cue explanations. Two text controls limit writing demands but leave reasoning partly in discussion. Fixed fixtures make consequences inspectable but restrict exploration. A single recovery snapshot is simpler but offers limited history.

This is the Learning scientist’s expert draft for the Evidence Studio lifecycle rehearsal. It challenges and extends the provisional Map artifact at sequence 15, drawing on the domain contribution at sequence 4, Human-centered designer contribution at sequence 6, Understand synthesis at sequence 8 and Systems engineer specification at sequence 13. These sources are project drafts, not participant observations, approved requirements or evidence of expertise. The parent iteration is background only. No scenario or technical finding was supplied; no scenario-driven change is claimed.

Problem and instructional purpose

The meaningful learner task is to decide what fictional records support and represent that position faithfully. Selecting an evidence pair identifies records to examine; it does not establish that the learner understands how those records relate to the claim. Likewise, retaining, narrowing, revising or withholding is an action, not an observable level of competence. A learner can revise through compliance or retain through careful reasoning.

Design should therefore expose a repeatable opportunity: inspect the selected records, consider the scope of the claim, choose what to do next and review the resulting record. This is an intended practice structure. Its usefulness, comprehensibility and learning effects remain untested.

Human and system capability

Human requirements: learners need intelligible evidence, time to compare, permission to disagree and accessible ways to contribute without typing. Facilitators need neutral prompts and workable discussion, language and scribing support. They must be able to pause disputed attribution without declaring an explanation correct or assuming everyone agrees. Reading fluency, device operation, silence and completion cannot substitute for reasoning evidence.

System requirements: the candidate must display the claim and selected pair together, describe recorded differences accurately and preserve unknowns. It must represent learner choices without inferring understanding, agreement or causal validity. It must preserve wording through explicit proposals and confirmation, support cancellation and correction, and retain the Map specification’s bounded recovery and confirmed handoff clearing. No additional required text entry, personal record, score, storage or telemetry is proposed.

D2 requirement 1 — Make claim/evidence comparison an actual interaction

Origin: Learning scientist, extending the domain’s claim-scope requirement at sequence 4 and the comparison and synthesis requirements integrated at sequences 8 and 15.

Interaction: beside the selected pair, show two compact areas: “Our selected claim” and “What these records say.” The latter contains exact descriptive comparison and relevant unknowns. Offer an optional disclosure, “Compare the claim with this pair,” with learner-selected descriptions such as “My claim describes these records,” “My claim goes beyond these records,” and “I have not decided how they connect.” These are descriptions selected by the learner, not verdicts supplied by the application. They can be changed or left unanswered without blocking progress. A claim that asks about causation may require discussion beyond these short options; the facilitator prompt should explicitly invite that question.

The concrete output is the selected claim beside the comparison, with any learner-selected relationship labeled as their current view. Changing the pair changes the factual comparison and makes the new pair visible. It must not automatically change the relationship selection or claim. If a relationship selection already exists, a neutral invitation to reconsider it may appear; no warning should imply that retaining it is wrong.

For A/B, the descriptive comparison states that B finishes 6 cm taller and both recorded water and light differ. For A/C, A finishes 2 cm taller, recorded light matches and recorded water differs. For B/C, B finishes 8 cm taller, recorded water matches and recorded light differs. Starting height, plant type and soil remain unrecorded in every original comparison. Final height is not growth; leaf appearance does not establish health. With only A/B revealed, confirming that pair is honestly presented as selecting the only available comparison.

Human reason: learners need an opportunity to examine claim scope rather than merely identify two cards. System reason: exact comparisons can support inspection without attempting to interpret arbitrary learner wording or produce an automatic correctness judgment.

Observable acceptance check: a reviewer chooses an own-worded claim, reveals C, switches among all three pairs and inspects the changing descriptive output. Claim wording remains unchanged. The reviewer can select, change or leave unanswered the relationship description and cancel an edit. No route produces a grade, causal endorsement or competence label. The main learner path still has at most two optional open-text controls. These checks are proposed and unperformed.

D2 requirement 2 — Make reconsideration deliberate and feedback descriptive

Origin: Learning scientist, strengthening the equal-status reconsideration and faithful-authorship requirements from the Human-centered designer at sequence 6 and the transactional specification from the Systems engineer at sequence 13, integrated into Map at sequence 15.

Interaction: introduce C as another fictional record that may complicate the explanation. Reveal it through a learner action and keep the earlier evidence accessible. Offer retain, narrow, revise and withhold with equal visual status. Selecting an action changes the displayed action label; it does not silently replace wording. Narrowing or revision can open the existing later-position control with a proposal clearly separated from the committed record. Confirm commits the reviewed wording; cancel preserves the previous record.

At synthesis, show the initial claim and pair beside the later action, position and pair. Feedback describes what changed: for example, “You kept the wording and changed the selected pair from A/B to A/C.” It must not say that a learner improved, corrected a misconception or demonstrated understanding. Withholding means a claim is currently withheld; it must not erase the earlier record or imply inability. Disagreement and representation remain separate from scientific reconsideration.

Human reason: deliberate practice requires an intelligible opportunity to reconsider a decision, while agency requires that no change remain a legitimate outcome. System reason: descriptive state comparison is inspectable; inferring the learner’s reason for a change is unsupported.

Observable acceptance check: exercise all four routes, including retaining wording while changing only the pair, withholding after an initial claim and canceling a proposed revision. Inspect both positions and the descriptive change statement. Confirm that a retained claim receives no adverse styling and a revised claim receives no reward or proficiency language. Correction and recovery must restore wording and associated selections together, following sequence 15. All checks remain pending.

D4 requirement 3 — Bound optional practice and reserve retention/transfer claims

Origin: Learning scientist, extending the supported-practice boundary in the Understand synthesis at sequence 8 and the W/L fixture mapping specified by the Systems engineer at sequence 13 and provisionally adopted at sequence 15.

Interaction: after the planning bench, offer a skippable “Try another prepared comparison” route using the other W/L fixture, with fewer claim suggestions. Keep the same opportunity to inspect recorded differences, discuss what remains unknown and retain, revise or withhold a position. Reuse existing controls rather than add required prose. Label this “Supported practice with another fictional comparison.” It occurs in the same session and retains substantial structural support; it cannot demonstrate retention or transfer.

The planning choice must still visibly select the correct prepared source: holding light constant and comparing water displays W1/W2, with final heights 11 and 13 cm; holding water constant and comparing light displays L1/L2, with final heights 9 and 14 cm. Recorded starting height, type, soil and duration match within each fixture as specified at sequence 13. Those authored fields do not fill gaps in A/B/C. Temperature and individual variation remain unrecorded; replication and allocation are unspecified. The fixed outcomes establish neither predictions nor causal rules.

For a future, separately reviewed evidence inquiry, delayed retention would require a later opportunity to make and explain a comparable decision after a specified interval. Transfer would require a meaningfully changed situation, such as a fictional non-plant comparison with different surface features and a new combination of recorded and missing conditions. Its materials, timing, assistance and interpretation criteria would need practitioner and affected-person review. A no-suggestion response is not automatically independent: facilitator cues, peer contributions, language support and task familiarity must be considered. Accessibility supports should not be withdrawn to manufacture independence.

Human reason: immediate supported performance and later performance answer different questions. System reason: a session completion record cannot establish either, and this candidate must not collect personal assessment data or infer proficiency.

Observable acceptance check: a reviewer can skip optional practice, complete it without additional required text, reconsider a choice and return to the correctable synthesis. Every practice display remains fictional and makes no transfer claim. Switching W/L changes identifiers, conditions, heights and comparison text together. Review of any future evidence plan must distinguish technical behavior, supported task performance, delayed retention and changed-context performance. No such observations or evidence plan approval exist.

Alternatives, dissent and rival explanations

The complete teacher-facilitated paper route is a non-AI alternative and may be the preferred design. It should reproduce the same claim/evidence comparison, separately revealed C, W/L planning choice, correctable before/after record and optional practice. Oral responses, a scribe, passing and separately recorded dissent must remain possible. The browser should not create an instructional decision that paper participants cannot make.

Retain the objections that C can feel like a trap, claim suggestions can cue explanations and a polished group synthesis can conceal ownership. This draft adds an optional, learner-described claim/evidence relationship and explicit descriptive change feedback; it does not claim these resolve the objections. If the added comparison controls burden reading or displace discussion, simplify them or use the equivalent oral prompt rather than add more fields.

Rival explanations for apparently successful performance include imitation, suggested-claim recognition, recall of fixture outcomes, adult cues and device-operator dominance. Apparent difficulty may reflect language access, unfamiliar units, navigation, time pressure or reasonable rejection of the framing. Neither completion nor revision distinguishes these explanations.

Evidence, unknowns and next decision

The supplied basis is the seed and earlier draft events 4, 6, 8, 13 and 15. Intended quality includes meaningful decisions, faithful feedback, correction, agency, dignity, access, belonging and sustainable workload. Observed technical behavior is absent. Learning, retention, transfer and flourishing evidence remain pending.

Teacher and support-staff review must examine instructional framing and workload; student review must examine comprehensibility, credible dissent and ownership; caregiver review must examine representation and shared-device expectations. These are proposed review responsibilities, not accepted assignments or approvals.

This is a Responsible AI specialist expert draft for the Evidence Studio rehearsal, not an approved requirement set. It extends the Human-centered designer’s authorship concerns at sequence 6, the Systems engineer’s state specification at sequence 13, the provisional Map synthesis at sequence 15 and the Learning scientist’s comparison interaction at sequence 20. The domain and Understand contributions at sequences 4 and 8 supply the fictional inquiry framing. These are project drafts, not participant observations, authorizations or demonstrated expertise.

The learner task remains helping a fictional garden team decide what its records support. Students, teachers, support staff and caregivers are intended or affected people, not participants in this demonstration. The responsible-AI concern is whether a polished shared record acquires more authority than its source warrants, and whether learners can control its visibility and correction when a shared device is interrupted or passed on.

Human and system capability

Humans retain authority over their wording, attribution requests and scientific interpretations. Operating the device grants permission to operate controls; it does not establish permission to speak for every learner. Facilitators support discussion, access and disputed attribution. They must not treat an interface selection as consent, settle the science question through the tool or use this candidate to automate assessment. Proposed reviewers may recommend revision, paper-only delivery or rejection. None has accepted a role or approved anything.

The system can display fixed fictional records, descriptive differences and deliberately selected positions. No AI inference is needed for this task. It cannot authenticate group agreement, detect coercion, establish equitable participation or determine why someone passes or revises. It must not generate grades, rankings, disability inferences or consequential reasoning scores.

Experience and decisions

Retain the short mission, A/B comparison, learner-triggered C reveal, prepared W/L planning choices and correctable before/after synthesis from sequence 15. Keep invented-data labels and interpretation limits beside the evidence. Suggested claims and the optional relationship descriptions proposed at sequence 20 remain prompts, not judgments.

Add a compact, consistently available “Cover activity” control for interruptions. Its screen offers “Resume this group” and “Clear for next group.” The first restores the same activity; the second opens the existing handoff confirmation. Keep help compact. A brief instruction near the optional wording controls should invite a claim without names or personal details. Do not add identity fields, another text entry or a participation log.

Requirements and rationale

RA1 — Keep delegated authority visible and contestable.
Origin: Responsible AI specialist, extending Human-centered designer sequence 6 and Systems engineer sequence 13, provisionally integrated at sequence 15.
Interaction: default representation to “One offered explanation.” Present agreement as “Selected description: agreed group explanation,” with a nearby statement that the activity does not verify agreement. Keep the independent disagreement marker and unresolved-discussion route. Agreement plus disagreement retains both selections and displays a neutral review request. Scientific reconsideration and attribution remain separate controls. Passing leaves existing contributions intact and creates no inferred agreement or participation tally.
Human reason: a learner must be able to reject attribution without being required to change the scientific claim. System reason: faithfully recording selections is narrower than establishing consensus.
Acceptance check: select agreement, mark disagreement, retain the claim after C and pass. Inspect the synthesis for the unresolved attribution notice and unchanged claim. Deliberately correct the representation. No output independently states that everyone agreed, that passing indicates inability or that revision demonstrates understanding. The social credibility of dissent remains an affected-person review question.

RA2 — Provide interruption concealment with an honest boundary.
Origin: Responsible AI specialist, extending shared-device conditions in the seed and handoff requirements at sequences 13 and 15.
Interaction: “Cover activity” hides the working interface behind a neutral screen. While covered, claims, drafts, dissent, summaries and recovery previews are absent from the visible and assistive-technology presentation; underlying controls cannot receive keyboard focus. Stop activity-derived announcements while covered. Place focus on the cover screen and restore a predictable, usable focus location on resume. Preserve pending and committed work exactly. Do not create a recovery snapshot merely for covering or resuming.
Human reason: an interruption should not force learners to choose between discarding work and leaving it immediately exposed. System reason: temporary concealment and clearing are distinct operations with different consequences.
Acceptance check: cover from a pending edit, synthesis and recovery preview. Inspect keyboard navigation and the accessibility presentation for concealed content, then resume and inspect preservation. These are planned checks, not results. The screen is not a lock: anyone with access can resume. Brief help must state this and the ordinary limits concerning screenshots, browser history, autofill and device records.

RA3 — Extend every state boundary to new Design interactions.
Origin: Responsible AI specialist, applying Systems engineer sequence 13 and Map sequence 15 to the relationship selections proposed by the Learning scientist at sequence 20.
Interaction: include every adopted initial, later or practice relationship selection in pending edits, committed state, recovery previews and confirmed handoff clearing. Changing an evidence pair updates the exact descriptive comparison but preserves the learner-selected relationship, as sequence 20 proposes; any invitation to reconsider stays neutral. Cancel preserves the committed record. Confirm commits only the reviewed proposal. Continue to distinguish original wording from explicitly corrected wording within the current group.
Human reason: authorship includes how learners describe the relationship between a claim and its evidence, not only their prose. System reason: an added control creates state that the older inventory did not explicitly name.
Acceptance check: select a relationship, change the pair, cancel an edit, commit a change and restore the single available snapshot. Inspect wording, pairs, relationship descriptions, representation and dissent together. Original and corrected wording remain distinguishable. No action silently rewrites the claim or interprets the relationship selection as correct. No earlier Map revision is requested; this is a Design extension to its existing state rule.

RA4 — Make recovery consequences and handoff clearing inspectable.
Origin: Responsible AI specialist, refining the bounded recovery and reset specification at sequences 13 and 15.
Interaction: recovery preview shows the proposed wording and associated selections, including any change in representation or dissent. A restored agreement label remains a selected, unverified description; recovery is not fresh agreement. Cancel preserves current work; restoration consumes the snapshot. From the cover screen or working activity, handoff confirmation explains that clearing removes this group’s work and recovery. Cancel returns to the preceding screen with all work preserved. Confirm clears committed and original/corrected records, drafts, relationship selections, pairs, reveal progress, plans, practice, representation, dissent, previews, input values and activity-derived announcements. Clear retained application references and return to an empty opening state. Public fictional source material may remain.
Human reason: recovery must not conceal a change in whose explanation is represented, and the next group must not inherit prior working content. System reason: hiding fields or resetting the main object alone is insufficient if other application layers retain the activity.
Acceptance check: populate every layer with distinctive fictional markers. Cancel handoff and inspect preservation; then confirm from an edit, cover screen, recovery preview and practice state. Inspect controls, rendered content, announcements and recovery for marker absence. Recovery must be unavailable. Code and interaction review must also check the prohibition on network, persistent storage, telemetry and external assets. No check has been performed, and clearing is not device-wide privacy certification.

Tradeoffs and alternatives

The complete teacher-facilitated paper activity is a non-AI option and may be the preferred outcome. It must preserve the mission, exact A/B/C records, staged reveal, W/L prepared comparisons, claim/evidence relationship prompt, before/after positions, correction and separate dissent. Oral or scribed participation and passing remain possible. A facilitator can set aside or cover paper during an interruption, but paper handling also needs human agreement; it is not automatically confidential.

Retain the objections that C may feel like a trap, claim suggestions may cue responses, and an agreed-group record may conceal refusal. A generic dissent marker protects against requiring another text entry but does not identify every disputed contribution. Where the shared record cannot faithfully represent the discussion, pause synthesis and use oral or paper facilitation rather than manufacture agreement.

The new interruption screen offers immediate visibility control at the cost of another interaction. Preserving original wording supports accountable correction but can prolong exposure of superseded wording within the group. If these arrangements are unacceptable or infeasible, simplify the activity, choose paper-only delivery or reject the candidate.

Acceptance checks

The requirement checks above are proposed review procedures, not completed verification. Implemented behavior would need keyboard, focus, accessibility-presentation and state-transition inspection. Testing must cover combined states, including disagreement plus agreement, a pending edit inside an interruption, and handoff while a recovery preview exists.

Technical success would establish only the inspected behavior under the tested conditions. It would not establish confidentiality, voluntary agreement, belonging, learning or transfer. No real student records should be introduced to test these mechanisms.

Evidence and unknowns

The supplied basis consists of the seed and earlier draft sequences 4, 6, 8, 13, 15 and 20. No scenario or technical finding was supplied. The changes proposed here follow design inspection: interruption handling was unspecified, and sequence 20 adds state that must inherit correction and clearing rules. No observed incident or scenario-driven change is claimed.

Unknowns include device arrangements, interruption frequency, browser behavior, languages, support availability, lesson duration and whether learners can credibly refuse attribution. Apparent success could reflect imitation, adult cues or operator dominance. Apparent difficulty could reflect language barriers, time pressure, navigation or reasonable rejection of the task. Revision and completion cannot distinguish these explanations.

Practitioner review of science framing, facilitation and workload; student review of access, privacy expectations and credible dissent; and caregiver review of representation and shared-device boundaries all remain pending. So do technical checks, human pilot work and all field evidence about agency, dignity, access, sustainable workload, belonging, learning and transfer.

This is the Learning engineer’s orchestrated Design brief for a lifecycle rehearsal. It integrates the domain contributor at sequence 4, Human-centered designer at sequence 6, Understand synthesis at sequence 8, Systems engineer at sequence 13, provisional Map synthesis at sequence 15, Learning scientist at sequence 20 and Responsible AI specialist at sequence 22. These are project drafts, not participant evidence or approved requirements. The parent school-science iteration is background only.

The task is to help a fictional school garden team explain what its available records support. Intended people are middle-school students with varied reading and language access, teachers and classroom support staff; caregivers are affected-person reviewers. None has participated in this demonstration. The design offers a meaningful decision about claim scope, followed by reconsideration and planning. It does not establish a student reasoning deficit.

Rival explanations for apparent difficulty include inaccessible language, unfamiliar units, navigation, time pressure, operator dominance and reluctance to disagree with an adult. Apparent success could reflect suggestion recognition, imitation, adult cues or familiarity with fixture outcomes. A learner may understand the uncertainty and reject the framing. Completion, fluency and revision cannot distinguish these explanations.

Human and system capability

Human requirements: learners need time and support to inspect records, discuss uncertainty and control their wording and attribution. Oral responses, another language, a scribe and passing must remain possible. Teachers and support staff need feasible discussion, language and device-turn routines, plus a way to pause disputed representation. Reader, operator and questioning voice are flexible invitations, not required roles or participation tests. Operating the device does not confer authority to speak for others.

System requirements: show exact fictional records and descriptive differences; preserve learner selections and wording; support explicit proposals, correction, cancellation, one recovery snapshot, temporary covering and confirmed handoff. No AI inference is needed. The candidate must not judge arbitrary claims, authenticate agreement, grade, rank, infer disability or assign proficiency. Use only in-memory activity state, with no network, storage, telemetry, external assets or real student records.

Proposed practitioner review covers science framing, fixture consistency, paper completeness and workload. Proposed student review covers comprehension, access, credible passing, dissent and attribution. Proposed caregiver review covers representation and shared-device expectations. These responsibilities are unaccepted and all review remains pending. Any assessment stays outside this candidate. No recruitment or classroom use is authorized by this rehearsal.

Experience and decisions

Opening: “Help the fictional garden team explain what its records support. Compare two records, offer a claim, then decide what another record changes.” Lead with a spacious evidence studio: A/B cards, a shared final-height graphic and one claim decision. Keep invented-data labels and interpretation limits beside the evidence. Put facilitation, paper materials and review status in compact expandable help. Cover activity and handoff remain easy to find without dominating the mission.

First decision: offer equally presented choices: “B finishes taller than A in these records”; “Water-2 plants always finish taller in this story”; “These records do not settle what caused the height difference”; own wording; or withhold. Identify these as starting suggestions, not verdicts. Confirm A/B honestly as the only available pair. Show the selected claim beside “What these records say.” Optional relationship choices are “My claim describes these records,” “My claim goes beyond these records,” and “I have not decided how they connect.” Label any selection as the learner’s current view. An unanswered relationship does not block progress.

Changed condition: introduce C with “Another fictional record may complicate the explanation. You can keep your position.” Reveal through learner action while retaining A/B. Now offer A/B, A/C and B/C through named pair controls. Changing the pair changes the descriptive comparison; it preserves the claim and relationship selection, with a neutral invitation to reconsider the relationship.

Planning: offer “Hold light constant; compare water” and “Hold water constant; compare light.” The choice displays the corresponding fixed W or L comparison, matching and differing recorded conditions, final-height difference and remaining unknowns. This is selecting a prepared example, not conducting an experiment or predicting an outcome. Additional proposed controls belong in discussion, without fabricated results.

Reconsideration: offer retain, narrow, revise and withhold at equal visual status. Selecting an action labels a pending proposal; it never silently changes wording. Retain proposes the current initial wording. Narrow and revise let the learner explicitly select a bounded observation or uncertainty suggestion, or use the later wording control. Withhold proposes no current claim while retaining the initial record. Review shows the exact proposed position, pair, relationship, representation and dissent before confirmation; cancel preserves the committed record.

Synthesis: show initial and later positions side by side, including pairs, learner-selected relationships and reconsideration action. Describe changes literally, such as “Wording retained; selected pair changed from A/B to A/C.” Do not describe improvement, misconception correction or demonstrated understanding. Include original and corrected initial wording when applicable. Default representation to one offered explanation; agreed group explanation and unresolved discussion require deliberate selection. An independent disagreement marker remains visible. Agreement plus disagreement displays a neutral representation-review notice while preserving both selections. Passing records no participation tally and changes no existing contribution.

Optional practice: after a planning choice, offer the other W/L fixture as “Supported practice with another fictional comparison.” Use fewer suggestions: the fixture-specific final-height observation, withhold, and an oral own-position route without another text field. Offer an optional relationship choice and retain/revise/withhold response; revision may explicitly select the alternative provided position. Keep practice separate from the A/B/C synthesis and make it skippable. Label the reduced response set as limited; a facilitator may use paper for fuller own wording. Same-session supported practice is not retention or transfer evidence.

Requirements and rationale

R1 — Focused comparison and faithful sources. Origin: domain sequence 4, Human-centered designer sequence 6, Understand sequence 8 and Map sequence 15. Use at most two optional main-path text controls, initial and later own wording, reused for correction. No typing is required. Final-height bars share a labeled 0–20 cm scale, numeric values and text equivalents; condition differences are expressed in words, never color alone. This limits entry burden while making the actual comparison inspectable. Check exact values, labels and every available pair as specified below.

R2 — Claim/evidence relationship and neutral reconsideration. Origin: Learning scientist sequence 20, extending sequences 4, 6 and 15. Place claim, selected pair, descriptive comparison and optional learner-selected relationship together. Pair changes preserve interpretation selections; action changes preserve committed wording until reviewed confirmation. This exposes claim scope without pretending to interpret arbitrary prose. Check own wording, all pairs, unanswered relationships and each reconsideration route without rewards or penalties.

R3 — Fixed planning consequences and bounded practice. Origin: Systems engineer sequence 13, provisionally adopted at sequence 15; Learning scientist sequence 20. Map the two supported planning choices exactly to W/L. Optional practice uses the other fixture and separate control-based state, with no third text field. This makes consequences concrete while avoiding an unsupported scientific calculator. Check W/L switching, restoration, separation from A/B/C and skippable practice.

R4 — Representation, dissent and human authority. Origin: Human-centered designer sequence 6, Systems engineer sequence 13, Map sequence 15 and Responsible AI specialist sequence 22. Display agreement as a selected, unverified description. Keep disagreement independent of science revision. Passing does not erase work or imply consent. This recognizes that recording choices is narrower than representing people. Check agreement plus dissent, deliberate representation correction and passing. Credible refusal remains a human-review question.

R5 — Transactional correction and recovery. Origin: Systems engineer sequence 13, Map sequence 15, Learning scientist sequence 20 and Responsible AI specialist sequence 22. Separate committed activity, pending edit and one pre-change recovery snapshot. A record edit includes wording, pair, relationship, action, representation and dissent. Confirm commits exactly the reviewed proposal; cancel discards it. Keep the first committed initial wording identifiable beside an explicitly corrected version.

Each committed activity change replaces the single snapshot with the preceding committed state, including wording versions, initial/later and practice selections, reveal progress, plan, representation and dissent. Draft keystrokes do not create history. Preview all consequential snapshot fields before restoring. Cancel preserves current work; restore replaces activity state and consumes the snapshot without creating a reverse snapshot. The snapshot contains no recursive recovery history. This makes the bounded repair promise inspectable. Check combined-state cancellation, correction and restoration.

R6 — Interruption and complete handoff. Origin: Responsible AI specialist sequence 22, extending Systems engineer sequence 13 and Map sequence 15. Cover activity removes working content from visible and accessibility presentation, prevents underlying keyboard focus and suppresses activity-derived announcements. Preserve committed work, pending drafts and recovery preview exactly; cover/resume creates no snapshot. Focus enters the neutral cover screen; resume returns to a usable prior control or stage heading. Offer Resume this group and Clear for next group. Cover is not a lock: anyone can resume.

Handoff confirmation states that clearing removes this group’s work and recovery. Cancel returns to the preceding screen, including a cover, pending edit or recovery preview, with work preserved. Confirm clears all committed records, original/corrected versions, drafts, relationships, pairs, actions, representation, dissent, reveal progress, plan, practice, previews, input values, activity-derived displays, announcements and retained application references. Return to an empty opening state; public fictional source material may remain. Recovery cannot cross handoff. Brief help explains that the activity cannot clear screenshots, browser history, autofill or other device records. Check all layers using fictional markers.

R7 — Access and complete paper delivery. Origin: domain sequence 4, Human-centered designer sequence 6, Systems engineer sequence 13 and Map sequence 15; extended by sequences 20 and 22. Use native named controls, keyboard operation, visible focus, readable responsive layout and non-color selection states. Reveal and planning updates need accessible notifications without unexpected focus movement. Text communicates all visual information. Supply the standalone paper sequence below, with the same claim/evidence and reconsideration decisions. This addresses browser access without assuming that facilitation resources exist. Check keyboard, enlarged text, narrow layout, accessibility presentation and paper-only facilitation.

Source and standalone paper package

Use this mission: “Help the fictional garden team explain what its records support. Compare A and B, offer or withhold a claim, then consider another record and a prepared comparison.” All cards are an invented 14-day story, not measurements, plant-care advice or real outcomes.

Opening cards: A — water 1 story unit/day; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves. B — water 2 story units/day; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves. Keep C on a separate reveal sheet: water 2 story units/day; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves. Starting height, plant type and soil are unrecorded for A/B/C. Final height is not growth; leaves do not establish health.

Paper visual specification: draw final-height bars on one 0–20 cm scale with ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20; label every bar with its identifier and exact centimetre value. Include these full text equivalents: A/B — B finishes 6 cm taller; water and light differ. A/C — A finishes 2 cm taller; light matches and water differs. B/C — B finishes 8 cm taller; water matches and light differs. Unrecorded conditions remain unknown in every pair. C challenges the universal water-2 claim; it does not establish an opposite causal rule.

Prepared W sheet: W1 and W2 each record starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil S, bright light and 14 days. W1 records water 1 story unit/day, final height 11 cm, upright leaves. W2 records water 2, final height 13 cm, upright leaves. Water differs; the other listed conditions match. W2 finishes 2 cm taller. Choose this sheet for Hold light constant; compare water.

Prepared L sheet: L1 and L2 each record starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil S, water 2 story units/day and 14 days. L1 records bright light, final height 9 cm, upright leaves. L2 records dim light, final height 14 cm, drooping leaves. Light differs; the other listed conditions match. L2 finishes 5 cm taller. Choose this sheet for Hold water constant; compare light.

Draw W/L bars on the same labeled scale with those text equivalents. Both sheets are additional authored fictional examples from sequence 13, separate from A/B/C. Temperature, individual variation and other conditions are unrecorded; replication and allocation are unspecified. Fixed differences establish neither causes nor predictions. Their recorded starting heights, type and soil do not fill original gaps.

Facilitator sequence: present mission and A/B; offer the opening claim choices above, own wording or withhold; confirm A/B and invite the optional relationship response. Ask neutrally, “What do these records say, and what does your claim add?” Introduce and reveal C without requiring change. Let learners select any available pair and reconsider its relationship to their claim. Offer the two planning choices and supply the selected W/L sheet. Invite additional control proposals orally without invented outcomes. Complete the later record, then optionally use the other prepared sheet for supported practice.

Paper record template: initial claim or withhold; initial pair A/B; optional relationship response. Later action retain/narrow/revise/withhold; later position or withhold; later pair A/B, A/C or B/C; optional relationship response. Representation: one offered explanation/agreed group explanation/unresolved discussion; independent disagreement: present/not marked. State that agreement is a selected description, not verified consensus. Provide original and corrected initial lines and review the before/after record before accepting changes. Optional practice has its own fixture identifier, selected position, relationship and reconsideration controls; it does not replace the original investigation.

Allow speech, another language, a scribe and passing without erasing contributions. For correction, show a proposed change separately and accept or cancel it explicitly. If paper recovery is desired, retain only one agreed checkpoint before the latest accepted change; review it before restoration and discard it afterward. Cover or set aside papers during interruption by human agreement. Paper handling and eventual disposal need an agreed routine; browser handoff does not clear paper. No participant names or real records are needed. Build must present these materials in a distinct paper/help view with usable print styling; paper-equivalence and preparation workload remain untested.

Tradeoffs and alternatives

Suggested claims ease entry but cue interpretations; two optional text controls reduce typing while leaving reasoning partly in discussion. Optional relationship prompts add inspectability but can be omitted or replaced by the equivalent oral prompt if they burden reading. Fixed fixtures constrain exploration and may cue a causal lesson despite their labels; reviewers may replace or reject them.

Retain objections that C can feel like a trap, one polished synthesis can conceal refusal, and device management can displace inquiry. Neutral reveal, visible representation and interruption controls are proposed responses, not demonstrated resolutions. No scenario was supplied, so no scenario-driven change is claimed. Changes since Map are the learner-selected relationship interaction and descriptive change feedback from sequence 20, plus cover/resume and expanded state coverage from sequence 22. They extend Design without invalidating an earlier artifact.

The teacher-facilitated paper activity is a complete non-AI alternative and may be preferred. Simplifying language, changing device arrangements, reducing scope, pausing disputed synthesis or rejecting the candidate are legitimate responses to unavailable support.

Acceptance checks

Content and decisions: inspect every source value and scale label; choose suggested, own-worded and withheld positions without required typing. Exercise A/B, A/C and B/C with unchanged wording and optional relationship selections. Follow all four reconsideration routes, including retain with a changed pair. Switch W to L and back; verify identifiers, constants, heights and descriptions together. Skip and revisit separate optional practice. No automatic verdict, growth/health inference or learning claim may appear.

State and privacy: cancel and commit edits; correct the initial record; preview, cancel and consume recovery while inspecting all associated fields. Exercise agreement plus dissent and passing. Cover from an edit, synthesis and recovery preview; inspect visibility, accessibility presentation, keyboard focus and exact preservation on resume. Populate every layer with distinctive fictional markers; cancel handoff, then confirm from edit, cover, recovery and practice states. Inspect controls, hidden content, announcements and recovery for marker absence. Review implementation for prohibited network, storage, telemetry and external assets.

Access and delivery: complete the task by keyboard; inspect focus, notifications, text-only interpretation, narrow layout and enlarged text; review assistive-technology interaction. A teacher reviewer should be able to facilitate the entire paper activity from its materials alone, including dissent, correction and optional practice. These procedures are planned; none has been performed.

Evidence and unknowns

Intended quality is a coherent, inspectable investigation with faithful authorship, agency, dignity, access, belonging and manageable workload. Observed technical behavior is absent. Technical verification would establish only the behavior inspected under tested conditions. It would not establish voluntary agreement, confidentiality, classroom suitability, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

Languages, reading supports, devices, browsers, time, interruption frequency, staffing, printing and preparation responsibility remain unknown. Practitioner and affected-person review, human pilot work and all field evidence remain pending. A future evidence inquiry would separately examine supported task performance, delayed retention and performance in a meaningfully changed context, documenting assistance and rival explanations without withdrawing access supports or collecting personal assessment data through this candidate.

Next decision

Proceed to Build one self-contained interactive candidate implementing this brief and the complete paper view. Inspect technical behavior before considering any human pilot. System requirements: display exact records and descriptive differences; preserve deliberate choices; distinguish correction, withholding, withdrawal, covering and handoff. Use explicit proposal review, cancellation and one bounded recovery snapshot. Add source-dependency bookkeeping for application-created copies without inferring authorship or semantic equivalence. No AI inference is needed. No real student records, automated grades, rankings, disability inference or consequential scores are permitted. Use no network, storage, telemetry or external assets.

Science practitioners and teachers would review framing, fixtures, paper completeness and workload. Students would review comprehension, access, credible passing, dissent and withdrawal. Caregivers would review representation and shared-device expectations. These proposed responsibilities are unaccepted; all review remains pending. Separate assessment stays outside the candidate.

Experience and decisions

Open with: “Help the fictional garden team explain what its records support. Compare two records, offer a claim, then decide what another record changes.” Show A/B, a shared final-height graphic and one claim decision. Keep fictional labels and interpretation limits beside evidence. Put facilitation, paper materials and review status in compact help.

Offer equally presented starting suggestions: “B finishes taller than A in these records”; “Water-2 plants always finish taller in this story”; “These records do not settle what caused the height difference”; own wording; or withhold. Confirm A/B honestly as the only available pair. Beside the claim show the descriptive comparison. Optional relationship choices are “My claim describes these records,” “My claim goes beyond these records,” and “I have not decided how they connect.” Label these as learner-selected views; leaving them unanswered does not block progress.

Introduce C neutrally: “Another fictional record may complicate the explanation. You can keep your position.” Learner-triggered reveal retains earlier cards and enables A/B, A/C and B/C selection. Pair changes update recorded differences while preserving wording and the selected relationship, with a neutral invitation to reconsider.

At the planning bench, choosing which recorded condition to hold constant displays fixed W or L records. This selects a prepared example, not an experiment or prediction. Then offer retain, narrow, revise and withhold at equal status. An action labels a proposal; it does not silently rewrite committed wording. Review exact wording, pair, relationship, action, representation and dissent before confirmation. Cancel preserves committed work.

The synthesis shows initial and later positions with literal change descriptions. Default representation to one offered explanation. Agreement and unresolved discussion require deliberate selection; agreement remains unverified. Keep an independent dissent marker. Passing preserves work without a tally or inferred agreement.

Add a named “Withdraw initial position” action beside its correction control. Review the removal scope and dependent consequences before confirmation. A withdrawn position becomes a content-free label, not a retained quotation. Dependent later wording needs a new deliberate choice; independent later work remains. Where removal authority or dependency is contested, pause and facilitate rather than certify permission through a click.

Optional supported practice uses the other W/L fixture, fewer suggestions and separate state. Offer its final-height observation, withhold or an oral own-position route, plus optional relationship and retain/revise/withhold controls. No third text field is needed. It is skippable and cannot establish retention or transfer.

Requirements and rationale

R1 — Focused evidence and faithful sources. Origins: domain sequence 4, Human-centered designer 6, Understand 8 and Map 15. Use at most two optional main-path text controls, initial and later wording, reused for correction. No typing is required. Final-height graphics share a labeled 0–20 cm scale with ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20, exact numeric values and text equivalents. Conditions and selection states use words, not color alone. Reason: reading stamina, typing and visual inference should not become hidden prerequisites. Check all values, pair descriptions and text equivalents; no height-as-growth or leaves-as-health labels may appear.

R2 — Inspectable claim scope and neutral reconsideration. Origins: Learning scientist 20, extending domain 4, Human-centered designer 6 and Map 15. Place claim, selected pair, exact comparison and optional relationship together. Pair changes preserve interpretation selections. Retain proposes current initial wording; narrow/revise require explicit suggestion selection or later own wording; withhold proposes no current claim while preserving history unless separately withdrawn. Reason: choices support examination without interpreting arbitrary prose or rewarding compliance. Check every route, own wording, unanswered relationships and retained wording with a changed pair. Feedback describes changes, never improvement or demonstrated understanding.

R3 — Fixed planning and bounded practice. Origins: Systems engineer 13, Map 15 and Learning scientist 20. “Hold light constant; compare water” selects W1/W2. “Hold water constant; compare light” selects L1/L2. Show matching/differing records, final-height differences and unknowns together. Keep optional practice separate from A/B/C. Reason: planning needs visible consequences without an unsupported calculator. Check W/L switching and exact restoration, unchanged A/B/C, skippable practice and no transfer claim.

R4 — Contestable representation. Origins: Human-centered designer 6, Systems engineer 13 and Responsible AI specialist 22. Agreement plus dissent preserves both selections and displays a neutral representation-review notice. Passing changes no contribution. Reason: recording selections cannot establish consensus or equitable participation. Check the combined state and deliberate correction without automatic attribution changes. Social credibility remains a human-review question.

R5 — Correction, withdrawal and dependency boundaries. Origins: Systems engineer 13, Map 15 and Responsible AI specialist 22; revised in response to Scenario 27 and Design 24. Ordinary correction preserves identifiable original wording only while that contribution remains active. Withdrawal is a separate reviewed transaction. Its preview identifies the selected initial contribution, all versions, associated relationship, application-created copies and affected later proposals. Cancel preserves committed state, drafts and recovery exactly.

On confirmation, remove that contribution’s wording and versions from records, inputs, drafts, previews, announcements and derived summaries. Clear its associated initial interpretation and replace its displayed position with “Initial position withdrawn.” Keep public fictional evidence, independent later contributions, planning, practice and dissent. A later retain copy or dependent proposal loses copied wording and shows “New position needed”; do not substitute another claim. Preserve independent representation selections as unverified descriptions, with a notice that the synthesis is now incomplete.

Track application-created dependencies through copying, correction and proposals. For ambiguous manually entered copies, the review must let people identify affected content or pause for facilitation; the system must not infer ownership from matching strings. Removal guarantees must be limited to the reviewed contribution and identified copies. It cannot discover every paraphrase or authenticate permission.

Reason: authorship includes contesting continued representation, while independent work also deserves preservation. Check cancellation, marker removal from every affected layer, dependency invalidation, preserved independent content and keyboard operation without another text field. Confirming scope is not proof of human authorization. Map must settle this revised authority and dependency boundary before Build.

R6 — Recovery, interruption and handoff. Origins: Systems engineer 13, Map 15, Responsible AI specialist 22; withdrawal exception from Scenario 27. Ordinary committed changes retain one preceding-state snapshot, including wording versions, pairs, relationships, actions, reveal, plan, practice, representation and dissent. Draft keystrokes create no history. Preview all consequential fields; cancel preserves current state; restoration consumes the snapshot without creating reverse history.

Withdrawal must not create a snapshot containing removed content. Sanitize affected records and dependent copies in the existing snapshot before it can be previewed or restored. Maintain a content-free withdrawal boundary outside ordinary undo so recovery cannot resurrect the withdrawn initial contribution. If sanitization cannot preserve a coherent snapshot, discard it and explain the lost recovery before confirmation. Later recovery remains subject to that boundary; handoff clears it. Check restoration after withdrawal, including a snapshot predating correction or a dependent retain proposal.

Cover activity removes work from visible and accessibility presentation, prevents underlying focus and suppresses activity-derived announcements. Preserve committed state, drafts and previews; cover/resume creates no snapshot. Focus enters a neutral screen and returns to a usable control or heading. Cover is not a lock: anyone can resume.

Confirmed handoff clears records, versions, drafts, dependencies, withdrawal boundary, relationships, pairs, actions, representation, dissent, reveal, plan, practice, previews, recovery, input values, announcements and retained application references. Cancel returns to the preceding activity, cover or preview with work intact. Brief help explains limits concerning screenshots, browser history, autofill and device records. Check all layers with fictional markers; recovery cannot cross handoff.

R7 — Access and complete paper delivery. Origins: domain 4, Human-centered designer 6, Systems engineer 13, Learning scientist 20, Responsible AI specialist 22 and Scenario 27. Use native named controls, visible focus, predictable keyboard order, readable responsive layout and accessible update notifications without unexpected focus movement. Every graphic has a full text equivalent. Reason: browser access is only one participation condition. Check keyboard completion, enlarged text, narrow layout and assistive-technology presentation. The standalone paper package below must support the same decisions; paper-equivalence and preparation workload remain untested.

Standalone source and paper package

All cards are an invented 14-day story, not measurements, plant-care advice or real outcomes. Opening A: water 1 story unit/day; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves. B: water 2 story units/day; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves. Separately revealed C: water 2 story units/day; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves. Starting height, plant type and soil are unrecorded. Final height is not growth; leaves do not establish health.

Draw labeled bars on the shared 0–20 cm scale. Full text comparisons: A/B — B finishes 6 cm taller; water and light differ. A/C — A finishes 2 cm taller; light matches and water differs. B/C — B finishes 8 cm taller; water matches and light differs. Unknown conditions remain unknown. C challenges the universal water-2 claim without establishing an opposite causal rule.

Prepared W sheet: W1/W2 both record starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil S, bright light and 14 days. W1: water 1 story unit/day, final height 11 cm, upright leaves. W2: water 2, final height 13 cm, upright leaves. Water differs; other listed conditions match; W2 finishes 2 cm taller. Select W for holding light constant and comparing water.

Prepared L sheet: L1/L2 both record starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil S, water 2 story units/day and 14 days. L1: bright light, final height 9 cm, upright leaves. L2: dim light, final height 14 cm, drooping leaves. Light differs; other listed conditions match; L2 finishes 5 cm taller. Select L for holding water constant and comparing light.

Use the same bar scale and text equivalents for W/L. These additional authored fixtures originate at sequence 13 and do not fill A/B/C gaps. Temperature, individual variation and other conditions are unrecorded; replication and allocation are unspecified. Fixed outcomes establish neither causes nor predictions.

Facilitator sequence: present mission and A/B; offer the opening claim choices, own wording or withhold; confirm A/B and optionally discuss the relationship. Ask, “What do these records say, and what does your claim add?” Introduce C without requiring change; let learners choose any pair. Offer the two planning choices and corresponding sheet, then review the later position. Optionally use the other fixture as supported practice. Additional proposed controls can be discussed without fabricated outcomes.

Paper record: initial claim/withhold and pair A/B; optional relationship; original and explicitly corrected wording while active. Later record: retain/narrow/revise/withhold, exact position, selected pair and optional relationship. Representation: one offered explanation/agreed group explanation/unresolved discussion; separate dissent present/not marked. Agreement is selected, not verified. Optional practice has a separate fixture, position, relationship and reconsideration record.

Allow speech, another language, a scribe and passing. Review corrections separately and accept or cancel. Keep at most one agreed paper checkpoint for optional recovery. For withdrawal, review selected lines, dependent copies and checkpoint; remove affected content by human agreement while preserving independent work. Dependent positions need a new choice. Ordinary crossing-out leaves words readable and must not be presented as removal. Paper handling, replacement sheets, copies and disposal need an agreed routine; browser clearing cannot control them. Cover or set aside papers during interruption. Build should include a distinct paper view with usable print styling; no participant names are needed.

Tradeoffs and alternatives

Retain objections that C can feel like a trap, suggestions can constrain interpretation, a polished synthesis can conceal refusal and withdrawal can remove useful reasoning history. Neutral reveal and explicit representation are proposed responses, not demonstrated resolutions. Sequence 27 changes mandatory retention into retention subject to reviewed withdrawal, and makes recovery subordinate to removal boundaries.

Selective removal adds complexity and possible misuse. When attribution or dependencies cannot be resolved, pause synthesis and use facilitated oral or paper discussion. Complete teacher-facilitated paper delivery is the non-AI alternative and may be preferred. Simplifying language, changing device arrangements, reducing scope, replacing fixtures or rejecting the candidate remain legitimate.

Acceptance checks

Content and decisions: inspect every source value and scale; exercise every claim, pair, relationship and reconsideration route without required typing. Switch W/L and skip or revisit separate practice. Verify descriptive feedback without grades, causal endorsement, health inference or learning claims.

State and removal: use fictional markers in original wording, correction, dependent later proposals, drafts and recovery. Cancel withdrawal and inspect exact preservation; confirm and inspect affected layers for absence. Restore sanitized recovery and verify no resurrection. Check independent work and dissent, new-choice prompts, ordinary cancellation/correction, cover/resume and full handoff from combined states.

Access and paper: complete the journey and withdrawal by keyboard; inspect focus, announcements, concealed accessibility content, narrow layout and enlarged text. A teacher reviewer should be able to facilitate the complete paper sequence, including removal and disagreement, from its materials alone. All checks are proposed and unperformed.

Evidence and unknowns

Intended quality includes meaningful inquiry, faithful authorship, agency, dignity, access, belonging and manageable workload. Observed technical behavior is absent. Technical verification would establish only inspected behavior, not voluntary agreement, classroom suitability, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

The hypothetical removal request could reflect misattribution, discomfort, changed interpretation or rejection of shared recording. It establishes neither coercion nor misunderstanding. Languages, devices, browsers, time, interruption frequency, staffing, printing and feasible dependency review remain unknown. Practitioner and affected-person review, human pilots and all field evidence remain pending. Later learning inquiry must separate supported performance from delayed retention and changed-context performance, document assistance and rival explanations, and retain access supports.
