This is the orchestrator’s working Understand artifact for a lifecycle rehearsal. It integrates the domain draft at sequence 4 and the Human-centered designer draft at sequence 6. These are provisional contributions, not approved requirements or participant evidence. The seed supplies the fictional investigation and constraints. The parent school-science iteration supplies background only. No technical checks, human approvals, classroom observations or learning outcomes have been supplied.

Problem and people

The proposed task is to help a fictional school garden team decide what its available records support. Learners choose a claim and an evidence-card pair, inspect recorded differences, encounter an additional record and decide how to represent their explanation afterward. The problem is an opportunity for evidence comparison and bounded explanation; a student reasoning deficit has not been established.

Intended users are middle-school students with varied reading and language access, science teachers and classroom support staff. Caregivers are affected-person reviewers. None are participants in this demonstration. A shared device makes participation and representation a group concern: operating the interface does not confer authority to speak for everyone.

Rival explanations for apparent difficulty include inaccessible language or unfamiliar units, confusing graphics or task navigation, time pressure, unequal device turns and reluctance to disagree with an adult. A learner may also understand the uncertainty while rejecting the framing. Neither completion nor fluent wording distinguishes these explanations. Understand therefore retains both interaction barriers and instructional framing as open explanations.

Source facts and interpretation boundaries

All observations belong to an invented 14-day story. A records water 1 story unit/day, bright light, final height 12 cm and upright leaves. B records water 2 story units/day, dim light, final height 18 cm and drooping leaves. C records water 2 story units/day, bright light, final height 10 cm and upright leaves. These are not measurements, plant-care advice or real outcomes.

Starting height, plant type and soil are unrecorded. Final height does not establish growth; leaf appearance does not establish health. A and B differ in both recorded water and light. A and C share recorded light and differ in recorded water, while unrecorded conditions remain unknown. B and C share recorded water and differ in recorded light. C challenges the universal descriptive claim that water-2 plants always finish taller in this story. It does not establish an opposite causal rule.

The seed requires two fixed fictional prepared comparisons for the test-planning bench but does not supply their complete records or choice mapping. Those examples are a Map dependency. They must be explicitly authored as additional invented examples, separately identified from A/B/C, and reviewed for consistency before Design or Build. They must not silently supply missing conditions for the original cards.

Human and system capability

Learners need opportunities to compare records, choose or supply a claim, select a pair, discuss uncertainty and reconsider without compulsory revision. Oral contributions, a scribe, another language, passing and dissent must remain possible. These supports depend on available people, time and materials; the interface cannot provide equitable participation by itself.

Teachers and support staff need manageable facilitation prompts and responsibility for language support, device turns and disputed attribution. Flexible roles such as evidence reader, operator and questioning voice may help, but rotation must not become a participation test. Any separate assessment remains a human responsibility outside this candidate; the tool must produce no automated grades, rankings, disability inference or proficiency judgment.

The system must make recorded conditions, fictional status and unknowns intelligible, preserve authored wording and display decision consequences descriptively. It must distinguish the initial record from subsequent proposals, avoid implied consensus and permit recovery from ordinary mistakes. Origin: domain contributor, sequence 4; Human-centered designer, sequence 6; integrated here by the Learning engineer. Begin with a short mission to advise the fictional garden team. Keep the main learner path to at most two open-text entries, neither required for progress. Use labeled final-height graphics on a consistent scale, centimetre values and text equivalents; show recorded water, light and leaf appearance in words. Requirement 2 — Neutral reconsideration with faithful authorship.
Origin: domain contributor, sequence 4; Human-centered designer, sequence 6. Introduce C as another fictional record that may complicate the explanation, then reveal it through a learner action. Keep the earlier comparison accessible and make C available for later pair selection. Offer retain, narrow, revise and withhold at equal status. The synthesis must show the initial claim and evidence beside the later position, action and evidence. Proposed wording requires explicit acceptance or editing; learner wording must never be silently replaced. Allow a learner-selected representation status: agreed group explanation, one offered explanation or unresolved discussion. Acceptance check: a reviewer can retain the original after C, change the pair, take every reconsideration route, record unresolved discussion, cancel a proposed edit and correct the final record. Origin: domain contributor, sequence 4; Human-centered designer, sequence 6. Reason: a planning interaction should expose a meaningful consequence while preserving the distinction between preparing a comparison and interpreting existing records.

This is a Systems engineer expert draft for the lifecycle rehearsal, not an approved specification. It responds to the domain draft at sequence 4, the Human-centered designer draft at sequence 6 and the Understand synthesis at sequence 8. These events supply proposed requirements, not participant evidence. The seed supplies A/B/C and the operating constraints. No technical checks, human approval or field results exist.

Problem framing and rival explanations — D1.problem

The task is to help learners represent what fictional garden records support. A reasoning deficit has not been established. Apparent difficulty could instead arise from inaccessible wording, unfamiliar story units, navigation, time pressure, unequal device control or reluctance to disagree with an adult. A learner may understand the uncertainty and reject the framing. Training learners to comply with the interface would not resolve these explanations.

The principal systems challenge is maintaining a faithful, revisable record while people share one device. Interaction authority and representational authority differ: operating a control does not establish permission to speak for others. The tool cannot authenticate agreement without introducing personal records or unsupported inferences. It should expose attribution choices and leave disputed agreement to human facilitation.

Requirement S1: visible, contestable representation

Origin: Systems engineer, extending sequences 4, 6 and 8. The final record must show a learner-selected representation status: one offered explanation, agreed group explanation or unresolved discussion. Default to one offered explanation; never infer agreement from completion, silence or passing. Provide a disagreement marker independent of claim revision. A disagreement marker combined with an agreement label must produce a neutral request to review the representation, not silently alter either selection. The group can choose unresolved discussion without adding text.

Human reason: learners need a practical way to contest attribution; a facilitator needs a way to pause recording without deciding whose science explanation wins. System reason: the application can faithfully display selections but cannot verify consent or consensus.

Observable acceptance check: a reviewer selects agreement, then marks disagreement; both remain visible until deliberately corrected, and the summary identifies the representation as needing review. Passing preserves existing contributions. No output states that all learners agreed as an independently verified fact.

Support dependency: credible dissent depends on adult conduct, group norms, language support and time. Student review of whether refusal feels possible remains pending. The product must not claim that a disagreement control establishes belonging or psychological safety.

Requirement S2: separately authored planning fixtures

Origin: Systems engineer, resolving a source-data dependency identified in sequences 4, 6 and 8. The following are proposed additional invented records for review. They are newly authored rehearsal fixtures, not supplied observations, measurements or extensions of A/B/C. Original starting height, plant type and soil remain unrecorded.

Fixture W — hold recorded light constant; compare recorded water.
W1: invented 14-day story; starting height 4 cm; fictional plant type T; fictional soil mix S; water 1 story unit/day; bright light; final height 11 cm; upright leaves.
W2: invented 14-day story; starting height 4 cm; fictional plant type T; fictional soil mix S; water 2 story units/day; bright light; final height 13 cm; upright leaves.
Descriptive output: recorded water differs; recorded light, starting height, type, soil and duration match. W2 finishes 2 cm taller in this prepared story. Temperature, individual variation and other conditions are unrecorded; replication and allocation method are unspecified. This difference does not establish what caused the outcome.

Fixture L — hold recorded water constant; compare recorded light.
L1: invented 14-day story; starting height 4 cm; fictional plant type T; fictional soil mix S; water 2 story units/day; bright light; final height 9 cm; upright leaves.
L2: invented 14-day story; starting height 4 cm; fictional plant type T; fictional soil mix S; water 2 story units/day; dim light; final height 14 cm; drooping leaves.
Descriptive output: recorded light differs; recorded water, starting height, type, soil and duration match. L2 finishes 5 cm taller in this prepared story. Temperature, individual variation and other conditions are unrecorded; replication and allocation method are unspecified. Leaf appearance does not validate health, and this difference does not establish causation.

Interaction mapping: offer two supported choices, “Hold light constant; compare water” and “Hold water constant; compare light.” The first selects W1/W2; the second selects L1/L2. Display the matching recorded conditions alongside the selected comparison. Do not imply that the learner has actually controlled conditions or conducted an experiment. If a learner wants to hold additional unrecorded conditions constant, a facilitation prompt can preserve that proposal; the application must not fabricate another example or calculated outcome.

Human reason: the learner can connect a planning choice to a visible comparison while questioning its limits. System reason: a fixed lookup is inspectable and avoids an unsupported plant-growth model.

Observable acceptance check: switching W to L changes card identifiers, exact records, graphics and difference text together; switching back restores W exactly. No unsupported control combination produces an outcome. Both fixtures retain invented-data labels and unknowns. A/B/C remain exactly as supplied, with their missing fields unchanged.

These fixtures are a reviewable proposal, not settled source authority. Domain and teacher review must examine whether their final-height differences inadvertently cue a preferred explanation. Rejection or replacement of the fixtures remains possible before Design.

Requirement S3: transactional editing and bounded recovery — D4.verification

Origin: Systems engineer, specifying the recovery requirement in sequences 4, 6 and 8. Distinguish the initial committed claim and pair, the later committed position and pair, and a pending edit. Use at most two optional text entries on the main path: initial own wording and later own wording. Evidence selection, representation and dissent use named controls. Selecting retain, narrow, revise or withhold must not silently rewrite either text entry.

An edit opens a pending proposal showing current and proposed content. Confirm commits exactly the reviewed proposal. Cancel discards the proposal and preserves the current record. An explicit correction to the initial record must identify the corrected version and keep the original visible within the current activity; it must not rewrite history as if the corrected text had always been entered.

Provide one clearly labeled within-group recovery snapshot of the state preceding the latest committed change. It includes claims, pairs, reconsideration action, reveal state, planning choice, representation, dissent and optional practice state. Preview the snapshot before restoring it; cancellation leaves the current state untouched. A successful restore consumes that snapshot, so the control does not promise an unlimited history. Draft keystrokes are not separate recovery entries.

Human reason: users need to repair accidental edits without losing authorship. System reason: explicit state boundaries prevent cancel, correction and recovery from having ambiguous effects.

Observable acceptance check: enter distinctive fictional wording, change the evidence pair, cancel an edit and inspect unchanged committed content. Commit a different proposal, preview recovery, cancel recovery, then restore it. Confirm that wording and all associated selections return together. Correct the initial record and verify that original and correction are distinguishable. No check has been performed.

Requirement S4: shared-device handoff clears every activity layer

Origin: Systems engineer, extending the seed and sequences 4, 6 and 8. Handoff requires a compact confirmation. Cancel preserves the entire activity. Confirm clears committed records, pending drafts, original/corrected versions, selections, representation, dissent, reveal progress, planning choice, optional practice and recovery. Clear application-owned input values, displayed summaries, announcements and retained state references. Only public fictional fixtures and an empty opening state remain.

The reset must work from an unfinished edit, a recovery preview and optional practice. Recovery cannot cross a confirmed handoff. No storage, telemetry or network is permitted; state is held only for the current in-memory activity. Reopening starts empty.

Human reason: the next group should not inherit the previous group’s wording or disputes. System reason: clearing only visible fields leaves hidden drafts and recovery available.

Observable acceptance check: populate every layer with distinctive fictional marker text, cancel handoff and verify preservation. Confirm handoff and inspect application controls, summaries, announcements, drafts and recovery for absence of the markers; recovery remains unavailable. Repeat from a pending edit and optional practice. These are proposed technical checks, not privacy certification or completed results.

Brief help must explain that clearing the activity does not control screenshots, browser history, autofill, operating-system features or other device records. Ordinary browser limits should not displace the learner mission.

Requirement S5: access and facilitation are coupled dependencies — D1.coupling

Origin: Systems engineer, operationalizing sequences 4, 6 and 8. All decisions must be keyboard operable with named controls, visible focus and readable selection states. Evidence graphics need consistent final-height scales, numeric centimetre labels and text equivalents. C must appear through an explicit reveal action with an accessible notification and predictable focus. Planning changes must announce which prepared comparison is displayed without moving the user away from the control.

Human requirements: available facilitation for discussion and disputed attribution; workable oral, scribed or multilingual contributions; permission to pass; sufficient time and materials. Teachers need flexible device turns that do not turn rotation into a participation test. These conditions are unknown, not assumed resources.

System requirements: low entry burden, no required typing, at most two main-path text entries, visible unknowns, equal-status reconsideration routes and a complete paper package. The paper package must contain the mission, exact A/B records, separately revealed C, labeled comparison visuals with text equivalents, both proposed fixtures and their choice instructions, and an initial/later claim-and-evidence record with representation and dissent choices.

Observable acceptance check: a reviewer completes the decisions by keyboard, can interpret every comparison using text alone and retains access at narrow width and enlarged text. A teacher reviewer can conduct the same sequence from paper alone without consulting browser controls. No accessibility, paper-equivalence or workload checks have occurred.

Non-training levers include simplifying instructions, choosing paper-only delivery, providing a scribe or translation support, adjusting lesson scope, changing device-turn arrangements and pausing disputed attribution. If these supports are unavailable, reduce scope or reject the browser activity rather than attribute difficulty to learner capability.

Authority, dissent and review gates

Learners retain authority over their wording and attribution requests. A facilitator supports discussion and correction; the interface must not assign them authority to infer agreement or grade reasoning. Proposed reviewers include science practitioners for framing and fixture consistency, teachers and support staff for workload and materials, students for access and credible dissent, and caregivers for representation and shared-device expectations. These are proposed responsibilities, not accepted assignments or approvals.

Retain the objections from sequences 4 and 6: C may feel like a trap, suggested claims may constrain interpretation, and a polished group record may conceal disagreement. This draft adds explicit attribution conflict handling, a source-separated fixture proposal and bounded recovery. No scenario event was supplied, so these changes respond to draft dependencies rather than an observed incident.

Next decision and evidence limits

Ask the Map synthesis to adopt, revise or reject the fixture records and state rules before Design. It must also identify feasible language support, browser/device conditions, lesson time, preparation responsibility and a human process for disputed attribution. Keep a complete teacher-facilitated paper activity as the non-AI alternative and a legitimate final choice.

Technical behavior will require implementation checks. Classroom access, agency, dignity, belonging and sustainable workload require practitioner and affected-person review. This is the Learning engineer’s orchestrated Map artifact for a lifecycle rehearsal. It integrates the domain contribution at sequence 4, the Human-centered designer contribution at sequence 6, the Understand synthesis at sequence 8 and the Systems engineer draft at sequence 13. These are project drafts, not participant observations or approvals. The parent school-science iteration is background only. No technical behavior, classroom suitability, learning, transfer or flourishing outcome has been demonstrated.

Map adopts the sequence 13 planning fixtures and state rules as provisional inputs to Design. Adoption makes the next draft concrete and reviewable; it does not certify the materials or settle their instructional suitability. No scenario or technical finding was supplied, and no earlier artifact requires revision on the available basis.

Problem, decisions and rival explanations

The learner helps a fictional school garden team decide what its records support. The central decisions are choosing a claim and evidence pair, examining recorded differences, considering an additional record, selecting a prepared comparison through a planning choice, and representing a correctable later position. The task concerns the scope of an explanation, not finding a winning plant or obtaining a preferred verdict.

A reasoning deficit has not been established. Apparent difficulty could reflect language access, unfamiliar units, navigation, limited time, group dominance or reluctance to disagree with an adult. A learner may also understand the uncertainty and reject the framing. Completion, fluent wording and choosing revision do not distinguish these explanations. Simplifying instructions, changing device arrangements, providing support, choosing paper or stopping are legitimate responses.

Human capability and authority

Learners need opportunities to inspect evidence, compare conditions, express uncertainty and reconsider without compulsory rewriting. Typing must not be necessary: oral discussion, a scribe, another language and passing are supported participation routes. Learners control their wording and can contest attribution. Operating the device does not confer authority to speak for everyone.

Teachers and support staff would facilitate discussion, language access, flexible device turns and disputed attribution. Proposed roles such as reader, operator and questioning voice are invitations, not a participation test. A facilitator can pause the record and help people represent disagreement; the tool must not imply that adult intervention verifies consent or settles whose explanation is correct. Any separate assessment remains outside this candidate, with no automated grades, rankings, disability inference or proficiency judgments.

Proposed practitioner review responsibilities cover science framing, fixture consistency, facilitation and paper completeness. Proposed student review covers comprehensibility, credible passing and dissent, access and attribution. Proposed caregiver review covers representation and shared-device expectations. These are unaccepted responsibilities, not assignments or approvals. Real use requires accountable human review; this rehearsal authorizes neither recruitment nor classroom deployment.

System capability and boundaries

The system supports descriptive comparison and faithful representation. It cannot establish group agreement, equitable participation, causal effects, learning or confidentiality outside its own activity state. It must preserve exact source values, distinguish supplied records from newly authored fixtures, and keep interpretation limits near relevant evidence.

Use only in-memory activity state. No network, persistent storage, telemetry, external assets or real student records are permitted. Keyboard operation, clear focus, readable responsive layout, named selection states and text equivalents are required. Help and review metadata should be compact; invented-data labels and consequential limits remain visible where interpretation occurs.

Source specification

The supplied A/B/C records remain an invented 14-day story. A has water 1 story unit/day, bright light, final height 12 cm and upright leaves. B has water 2 story units/day, dim light, final height 18 cm and drooping leaves. C has water 2 story units/day, bright light, final height 10 cm and upright leaves. Starting height, plant type and soil are unrecorded for all three. Final height is not growth; leaf appearance does not validate health. These records are not measurements, plant-care advice or real outcomes.

A/B differ in recorded water and light; B finishes 6 cm taller. A/C share recorded light and differ in water; A finishes 2 cm taller. B/C share recorded water and differ in light; B finishes 8 cm taller. All comparisons retain the original unknowns. C challenges a universal claim that water-2 plants always finish taller in this story, but does not establish the opposite causal rule.

Planning fixture W, authored at sequence 13: W1 and W2 each have a recorded starting height of 4 cm, fictional plant type T, fictional soil mix S, bright light and an invented duration of 14 days. W1 has water 1 story unit/day, final height 11 cm and upright leaves. W2 has water 2 story units/day, final height 13 cm and upright leaves. Recorded water differs; the other listed conditions match. W2 finishes 2 cm taller in this prepared story.

Planning fixture L, authored at sequence 13: L1 and L2 each have a recorded starting height of 4 cm, fictional plant type T, fictional soil mix S, water 2 story units/day and an invented duration of 14 days. L1 has bright light, final height 9 cm and upright leaves. L2 has dim light, final height 14 cm and drooping leaves. Recorded light differs; the other listed conditions match. L2 finishes 5 cm taller in this prepared story.

Both fixtures are additional authored examples, separate from A/B/C. They do not fill missing original fields. Temperature, individual variation and other conditions are unrecorded; replication and allocation method are unspecified. The outcomes establish neither causation nor predictions. Their directions must not become lessons that more water or dim light produces taller plants. Domain and teacher review may replace or reject either fixture before real use.

Coupled requirements and acceptance checks

R1 — Focused entry and inspectable comparison. Origin: domain, sequence 4; Human-centered designer, sequence 6; Understand synthesis, sequence 8. Open with a short mission to help the fictional garden team explain what its records support. Begin with A/B, a claim choice and pair selection. Suggested claims may include a bounded observation, a broader claim to investigate and a statement of causal uncertainty; own wording and withholding remain available without a preferred-answer hierarchy. With only A/B revealed, A/B is the sole available pair: present its selection honestly as confirming the initial comparison. After C, pair selection becomes a choice among A/B, A/C and B/C.

Reason: entry should depend on an intelligible decision, not writing stamina or an appearance of choice. Use at most two optional main-path text controls, one for initial own wording and one for later own wording. Evidence graphics use a consistent final-height scale with centimetre values and full text equivalents. Show water, light, leaf appearance, fictional status and unknowns in words.

Acceptance check: a reviewer can choose or withhold a claim and confirm A/B without typing, then choose every available pair after C. Values and difference descriptions match the source specification. Graphics do not rename final height as growth or leaves as health. These checks are planned, not performed.

R2 — Neutral reveal and correctable synthesis. Origin: domain, sequence 4; Human-centered designer, sequence 6; Systems engineer, sequence 13. Introduce C as another fictional record that may complicate the explanation and reveal it through a learner action. Keep earlier evidence accessible. Offer retain, narrow, revise and withhold at equal status. Show initial claim and pair beside the later action, position and pair. Descriptive feedback reports records and differences; it does not judge whether the selected pair proves the claim.

Reason: reconsideration must remain an opportunity to examine scope, not obedience to a hidden answer. An action selection must never silently rewrite wording. If narrower or revised wording is proposed, show it separately for explicit acceptance or editing. Changing the evidence pair can be meaningful even when wording is retained.

Acceptance check: exercise all four routes, retain wording after C, change only the pair, withhold a later claim, and cancel a proposed rewrite. Original wording remains identifiable, and no route produces a score, causal endorsement or preferred-answer verdict. Whether these choices feel credible remains a student-review question.

R3 — Visible representation and dissent. Origin: Human-centered designer, sequence 6; Systems engineer, sequence 13. Default representation to one offered explanation. Allow deliberate selection of an agreed group explanation or unresolved discussion, alongside an independent disagreement marker. Label agreement as the group's selected description, not verified consensus. Agreement plus disagreement preserves both selections and displays a neutral request to review representation; it does not silently change either control. Passing must not imply agreement or erase existing contributions.

Reason: system interaction authority is narrower than authority to represent people. A compact shared record needs explicit limits and a human route for disputed attribution.

Acceptance check: select agreement, mark disagreement and inspect the conflict notice; deliberately choose unresolved discussion and verify the correction. Passing preserves existing work. No output independently asserts that every learner agreed. Credible dissent still depends on facilitation and group conditions.

R4 — Planning choices with visible consequences. Origin: domain, sequence 4; Human-centered designer, sequence 6; fixture proposal and mapping from Systems engineer, sequence 13. Offer exactly two supported choices: Hold light constant; compare water selects W1/W2. Hold water constant; compare light selects L1/L2. Display the chosen plan, fixed records, matching and differing recorded conditions, final-height difference and remaining unknowns together. Do not offer arbitrary combinations, calculated outcomes or language implying that the learner conducted an experiment. Additional proposed controls can be discussed with the facilitator without fabricated results.

Reason: a planning choice should visibly change the comparison while preserving the distinction between a prepared story and a conducted test.

Acceptance check: switch W to L and back; identifiers, values, graphics and descriptive text change together and restore exactly. A/B/C remain unchanged. The optional practice route may use the other prepared fixture with fewer claim suggestions and control-based responses, keeping the two main-path text controls unchanged. Label it supported practice in a changed comparison, make it skippable, and make no transfer claim.

R5 — Editing, correction and bounded recovery. Origin: correction requirements at sequences 4, 6 and 8; transactional specification from Systems engineer, sequence 13. Separate committed initial and later records from a pending proposal. Editing reuses the two optional text controls. Confirm commits the reviewed content; cancel discards pending changes and preserves committed content. A correction to the initial record shows its original version beside the corrected version within the activity, rather than rewriting history.

Keep one recovery snapshot from immediately before the latest committed change, covering wording and versions, pairs, reconsideration action, reveal progress, planning choice, representation, dissent and optional practice. Preview before restoration. Cancel preserves current state; restore replaces the activity with the previewed snapshot and consumes it without creating a reverse snapshot. Draft keystrokes do not create history. Label the scope clearly as recovery of the last committed change within this group.

Reason: wording and associated choices must recover together; a misleading undo promise could undermine authorship.

Acceptance check: cancel an edit, commit a different proposal, cancel recovery, then restore it. Inspect wording and every associated selection together. Correct the initial record and verify distinguishable original/corrected versions. A consumed snapshot cannot be restored again. No check has occurred.

R6 — Complete confirmed handoff. Origin: seed; sequences 4, 6 and 8; Systems engineer, sequence 13. Handoff uses a compact confirmation. Cancel preserves committed and pending work. Confirm returns to an empty opening state and clears committed records, original/corrected versions, drafts, selections, representation, dissent, reveal progress, plan, practice and recovery. Clear activity-derived displays, input values, announcements and retained state references; only public fictional source material remains. Recovery must not cross handoff.

Reason: clearing visible fields alone would leave prior-group information in other activity layers. Brief help explains that the application cannot clear screenshots, browser history, autofill or other device records.

Acceptance check: populate every layer with distinctive fictional marker wording; cancel handoff and inspect preservation. Confirm from an edit, recovery preview and practice state; markers are absent from application controls, displays, announcements and recovery. Recovery is unavailable. This is a proposed technical check, not privacy certification.

R7 — Access and complete non-AI delivery. Origin: domain, sequence 4; Human-centered designer, sequence 6; Systems engineer, sequence 13. Every decision needs keyboard operation, visible focus, named controls and selection states. Reveal and planning changes need accessible notifications and predictable focus. Text must communicate everything represented visually. Provide a complete teacher-facilitated paper package containing the mission, exact A/B cards, separately revealed C, comparison visuals and text equivalents, W/L fixtures and choice instructions, and initial/later claim-and-pair records with reconsideration, representation and dissent choices. Include oral or scribed participation, passing and correction instructions.

Reason: browser access is only one participation condition. Paper-only delivery is a complete non-AI option and may be preferable; teachers must not reconstruct the activity from controls.

Acceptance check: complete the journey by keyboard, inspect text-only interpretation, narrow layout and enlarged text, and review assistive-technology interaction. A teacher reviewer should be able to facilitate the full paper sequence using its materials alone. These checks and paper-equivalence review remain pending.

Dependencies, support and stopping conditions

Target languages, reading supports, devices, browsers, lesson duration, staffing, printing and preparation responsibility remain unknown. Design can specify a candidate under explicit assumptions; it cannot claim those conditions exist. Before any pilot, proposed responsible humans must establish feasible support and workload, review the materials and decide whether disputed attribution has a credible resolution process.

If support is unavailable, reduce scope, alter facilitation, choose paper-only delivery or reject the candidate rather than infer learner incapability. Do not treat flexible roles, a disagreement control or an attractive interface as evidence of belonging or equitable participation.

Tradeoffs and retained dissent

Suggested claims lower entry burden but can cue explanations. Two text controls limit writing demands but leave reasoning partly in discussion. Fixed fixtures make consequences inspectable but restrict exploration. A single recovery snapshot is simpler but offers limited history.

Retain the objections that C can feel like a trap, a polished record can misattribute agreement, and device management can displace inquiry. Neutral reveal, explicit representation and the paper route are proposed responses, not demonstrated resolutions. No scenario-driven change is claimed. Map changes resolve draft dependencies through source-separated fixtures, attribution conflict handling and explicit state boundaries.

Evidence and next decision

Supplied evidence consists of project drafts at sequences 4, 6, 8 and 13 and the seed. Fixture values are authored rehearsal data. Intended qualities include inspectable decisions, faithful correction, agency, dignity, access, belonging and manageable workload. Observed technical behavior and all human outcomes are absent.

Technical verification would establish whether implemented controls behave as specified, not learning. Human review would examine instructional meaning, access, attribution and workload. Any later inquiry into learning should distinguish supported task performance from delayed retention or performance in a changed context, documenting assistance and plausible rival explanations. All field evidence remains pending.

Proceed to Design with this provisional Map specification. This is the Learning scientist’s expert draft for the Evidence Studio lifecycle rehearsal. It challenges and extends the provisional Map artifact at sequence 15, drawing on the domain contribution at sequence 4, Human-centered designer contribution at sequence 6, Understand synthesis at sequence 8 and Systems engineer specification at sequence 13. These sources are project drafts, not participant observations, approved requirements or evidence of expertise. The parent iteration is background only. No scenario or technical finding was supplied; no scenario-driven change is claimed.

Problem and instructional purpose

The meaningful learner task is to decide what fictional records support and represent that position faithfully. Selecting an evidence pair identifies records to examine; it does not establish that the learner understands how those records relate to the claim. Likewise, retaining, narrowing, revising or withholding is an action, not an observable level of competence. A learner can revise through compliance or retain through careful reasoning.

Design should therefore expose a repeatable opportunity: inspect the selected records, consider the scope of the claim, choose what to do next and review the resulting record. This is an intended practice structure. Its usefulness, comprehensibility and learning effects remain untested.

Human and system capability

Human requirements: learners need intelligible evidence, time to compare, permission to disagree and accessible ways to contribute without typing. Facilitators need neutral prompts and workable discussion, language and scribing support. They must be able to pause disputed attribution without declaring an explanation correct or assuming everyone agrees. Reading fluency, device operation, silence and completion cannot substitute for reasoning evidence.

System requirements: the candidate must display the claim and selected pair together, describe recorded differences accurately and preserve unknowns. It must represent learner choices without inferring understanding, agreement or causal validity. It must preserve wording through explicit proposals and confirmation, support cancellation and correction, and retain the Map specification’s bounded recovery and confirmed handoff clearing. No additional required text entry, personal record, score, storage or telemetry is proposed.

D2 requirement 1 — Make claim/evidence comparison an actual interaction

Origin: Learning scientist, extending the domain’s claim-scope requirement at sequence 4 and the comparison and synthesis requirements integrated at sequences 8 and 15.

Interaction: beside the selected pair, show two compact areas: “Our selected claim” and “What these records say.” The latter contains exact descriptive comparison and relevant unknowns. Offer an optional disclosure, “Compare the claim with this pair,” with learner-selected descriptions such as “My claim describes these records,” “My claim goes beyond these records,” and “I have not decided how they connect.” These are descriptions selected by the learner, not verdicts supplied by the application. They can be changed or left unanswered without blocking progress. A claim that asks about causation may require discussion beyond these short options; the facilitator prompt should explicitly invite that question.

The concrete output is the selected claim beside the comparison, with any learner-selected relationship labeled as their current view. Changing the pair changes the factual comparison and makes the new pair visible. It must not automatically change the relationship selection or claim. If a relationship selection already exists, a neutral invitation to reconsider it may appear; no warning should imply that retaining it is wrong.

For A/B, the descriptive comparison states that B finishes 6 cm taller and both recorded water and light differ. For A/C, A finishes 2 cm taller, recorded light matches and recorded water differs. For B/C, B finishes 8 cm taller, recorded water matches and recorded light differs. Starting height, plant type and soil remain unrecorded in every original comparison. Final height is not growth; leaf appearance does not establish health. With only A/B revealed, confirming that pair is honestly presented as selecting the only available comparison.

Human reason: learners need an opportunity to examine claim scope rather than merely identify two cards. System reason: exact comparisons can support inspection without attempting to interpret arbitrary learner wording or produce an automatic correctness judgment.

Observable acceptance check: a reviewer chooses an own-worded claim, reveals C, switches among all three pairs and inspects the changing descriptive output. Claim wording remains unchanged. The reviewer can select, change or leave unanswered the relationship description and cancel an edit. No route produces a grade, causal endorsement or competence label. The main learner path still has at most two optional open-text controls. These checks are proposed and unperformed.

D2 requirement 2 — Make reconsideration deliberate and feedback descriptive

Origin: Learning scientist, strengthening the equal-status reconsideration and faithful-authorship requirements from the Human-centered designer at sequence 6 and the transactional specification from the Systems engineer at sequence 13, integrated into Map at sequence 15.

Interaction: introduce C as another fictional record that may complicate the explanation. Reveal it through a learner action and keep the earlier evidence accessible. Offer retain, narrow, revise and withhold with equal visual status. Selecting an action changes the displayed action label; it does not silently replace wording. Narrowing or revision can open the existing later-position control with a proposal clearly separated from the committed record. Confirm commits the reviewed wording; cancel preserves the previous record.

At synthesis, show the initial claim and pair beside the later action, position and pair. Feedback describes what changed: for example, “You kept the wording and changed the selected pair from A/B to A/C.” It must not say that a learner improved, corrected a misconception or demonstrated understanding. Withholding means a claim is currently withheld; it must not erase the earlier record or imply inability. Disagreement and representation remain separate from scientific reconsideration.

Human reason: deliberate practice requires an intelligible opportunity to reconsider a decision, while agency requires that no change remain a legitimate outcome. System reason: descriptive state comparison is inspectable; inferring the learner’s reason for a change is unsupported.

Observable acceptance check: exercise all four routes, including retaining wording while changing only the pair, withholding after an initial claim and canceling a proposed revision. Inspect both positions and the descriptive change statement. Confirm that a retained claim receives no adverse styling and a revised claim receives no reward or proficiency language. Correction and recovery must restore wording and associated selections together, following sequence 15. All checks remain pending.

D4 requirement 3 — Bound optional practice and reserve retention/transfer claims

Origin: Learning scientist, extending the supported-practice boundary in the Understand synthesis at sequence 8 and the W/L fixture mapping specified by the Systems engineer at sequence 13 and provisionally adopted at sequence 15.

Interaction: after the planning bench, offer a skippable “Try another prepared comparison” route using the other W/L fixture, with fewer claim suggestions. Keep the same opportunity to inspect recorded differences, discuss what remains unknown and retain, revise or withhold a position. Reuse existing controls rather than add required prose. Label this “Supported practice with another fictional comparison.” It occurs in the same session and retains substantial structural support; it cannot demonstrate retention or transfer.

The planning choice must still visibly select the correct prepared source: holding light constant and comparing water displays W1/W2, with final heights 11 and 13 cm; holding water constant and comparing light displays L1/L2, with final heights 9 and 14 cm. Recorded starting height, type, soil and duration match within each fixture as specified at sequence 13. Those authored fields do not fill gaps in A/B/C. Temperature and individual variation remain unrecorded; replication and allocation are unspecified. The fixed outcomes establish neither predictions nor causal rules.

For a future, separately reviewed evidence inquiry, delayed retention would require a later opportunity to make and explain a comparable decision after a specified interval. Transfer would require a meaningfully changed situation, such as a fictional non-plant comparison with different surface features and a new combination of recorded and missing conditions. Its materials, timing, assistance and interpretation criteria would need practitioner and affected-person review. A no-suggestion response is not automatically independent: facilitator cues, peer contributions, language support and task familiarity must be considered. Accessibility supports should not be withdrawn to manufacture independence.

Human reason: immediate supported performance and later performance answer different questions. System reason: a session completion record cannot establish either, and this candidate must not collect personal assessment data or infer proficiency.

Observable acceptance check: a reviewer can skip optional practice, complete it without additional required text, reconsider a choice and return to the correctable synthesis. Every practice display remains fictional and makes no transfer claim. Switching W/L changes identifiers, conditions, heights and comparison text together. Review of any future evidence plan must distinguish technical behavior, supported task performance, delayed retention and changed-context performance. No such observations or evidence plan approval exist.

Alternatives, dissent and rival explanations

The complete teacher-facilitated paper route is a non-AI alternative and may be the preferred design. It should reproduce the same claim/evidence comparison, separately revealed C, W/L planning choice, correctable before/after record and optional practice. Oral responses, a scribe, passing and separately recorded dissent must remain possible. The browser should not create an instructional decision that paper participants cannot make.

Retain the objections that C can feel like a trap, claim suggestions can cue explanations and a polished group synthesis can conceal ownership. This draft adds an optional, learner-described claim/evidence relationship and explicit descriptive change feedback; it does not claim these resolve the objections. If the added comparison controls burden reading or displace discussion, simplify them or use the equivalent oral prompt rather than add more fields.

Rival explanations for apparently successful performance include imitation, suggested-claim recognition, recall of fixture outcomes, adult cues and device-operator dominance. Apparent difficulty may reflect language access, unfamiliar units, navigation, time pressure or reasonable rejection of the framing. Neither completion nor revision distinguishes these explanations.

Evidence, unknowns and next decision

The supplied basis is the seed and earlier draft events 4, 6, 8, 13 and 15. Intended quality includes meaningful decisions, faithful feedback, correction, agency, dignity, access, belonging and sustainable workload. Observed technical behavior is absent. Learning, retention, transfer and flourishing evidence remain pending.

Target languages, feasible discussion time, assistance, device arrangements and paper preparation workload are unknown. Teacher and support-staff review must examine instructional framing and workload; student review must examine comprehensibility, credible dissent and ownership; caregiver review must examine representation and shared-device expectations. These are proposed review responsibilities, not accepted assignments or approvals.

This is a Responsible AI specialist expert draft for the Evidence Studio rehearsal, not an approved requirement set. It extends the Human-centered designer’s authorship concerns at sequence 6, the Systems engineer’s state specification at sequence 13, the provisional Map synthesis at sequence 15 and the Learning scientist’s comparison interaction at sequence 20. The domain and Understand contributions at sequences 4 and 8 supply the fictional inquiry framing. These are project drafts, not participant observations, authorizations or demonstrated expertise.

The learner task remains helping a fictional garden team decide what its records support. Students, teachers, support staff and caregivers are intended or affected people, not participants in this demonstration. The responsible-AI concern is whether a polished shared record acquires more authority than its source warrants, and whether learners can control its visibility and correction when a shared device is interrupted or passed on.

Human and system capability

Humans retain authority over their wording, attribution requests and scientific interpretations. Operating the device grants permission to operate controls; it does not establish permission to speak for every learner. Facilitators support discussion, access and disputed attribution. They must not treat an interface selection as consent, settle the science question through the tool or use this candidate to automate assessment. Proposed reviewers may recommend revision, paper-only delivery or rejection. None has accepted a role or approved anything.

The system can display fixed fictional records, descriptive differences and deliberately selected positions. No AI inference is needed for this task. It cannot authenticate group agreement, detect coercion, establish equitable participation or determine why someone passes or revises. It must not generate grades, rankings, disability inferences or consequential reasoning scores.

Experience and decisions

Retain the short mission, A/B comparison, learner-triggered C reveal, prepared W/L planning choices and correctable before/after synthesis from sequence 15. Keep invented-data labels and interpretation limits beside the evidence. Suggested claims and the optional relationship descriptions proposed at sequence 20 remain prompts, not judgments.

Add a compact, consistently available “Cover activity” control for interruptions. Its screen offers “Resume this group” and “Clear for next group.” The first restores the same activity; the second opens the existing handoff confirmation. Keep help compact. A brief instruction near the optional wording controls should invite a claim without names or personal details. Do not add identity fields, another text entry or a participation log.

Requirements and rationale

RA1 — Keep delegated authority visible and contestable.
Origin: Responsible AI specialist, extending Human-centered designer sequence 6 and Systems engineer sequence 13, provisionally integrated at sequence 15.
Interaction: default representation to “One offered explanation.” Present agreement as “Selected description: agreed group explanation,” with a nearby statement that the activity does not verify agreement. Keep the independent disagreement marker and unresolved-discussion route. Agreement plus disagreement retains both selections and displays a neutral review request. Scientific reconsideration and attribution remain separate controls. Passing leaves existing contributions intact and creates no inferred agreement or participation tally.
Human reason: a learner must be able to reject attribution without being required to change the scientific claim. System reason: faithfully recording selections is narrower than establishing consensus.
Acceptance check: select agreement, mark disagreement, retain the claim after C and pass. Inspect the synthesis for the unresolved attribution notice and unchanged claim. Deliberately correct the representation. No output independently states that everyone agreed, that passing indicates inability or that revision demonstrates understanding. The social credibility of dissent remains an affected-person review question.

RA2 — Provide interruption concealment with an honest boundary.
Origin: Responsible AI specialist, extending shared-device conditions in the seed and handoff requirements at sequences 13 and 15.
Interaction: “Cover activity” hides the working interface behind a neutral screen. While covered, claims, drafts, dissent, summaries and recovery previews are absent from the visible and assistive-technology presentation; underlying controls cannot receive keyboard focus. Stop activity-derived announcements while covered. Place focus on the cover screen and restore a predictable, usable focus location on resume. Preserve pending and committed work exactly. Do not create a recovery snapshot merely for covering or resuming.
Human reason: an interruption should not force learners to choose between discarding work and leaving it immediately exposed. System reason: temporary concealment and clearing are distinct operations with different consequences.
Acceptance check: cover from a pending edit, synthesis and recovery preview. Inspect keyboard navigation and the accessibility presentation for concealed content, then resume and inspect preservation. These are planned checks, not results. The screen is not a lock: anyone with access can resume. Brief help must state this and the ordinary limits concerning screenshots, browser history, autofill and device records.

RA3 — Extend every state boundary to new Design interactions.
Origin: Responsible AI specialist, applying Systems engineer sequence 13 and Map sequence 15 to the relationship selections proposed by the Learning scientist at sequence 20.
Interaction: include every adopted initial, later or practice relationship selection in pending edits, committed state, recovery previews and confirmed handoff clearing. Changing an evidence pair updates the exact descriptive comparison but preserves the learner-selected relationship, as sequence 20 proposes; any invitation to reconsider stays neutral. Cancel preserves the committed record. Confirm commits only the reviewed proposal. Continue to distinguish original wording from explicitly corrected wording within the current group.
Human reason: authorship includes how learners describe the relationship between a claim and its evidence, not only their prose. System reason: an added control creates state that the older inventory did not explicitly name.
Acceptance check: select a relationship, change the pair, cancel an edit, commit a change and restore the single available snapshot. Inspect wording, pairs, relationship descriptions, representation and dissent together. Original and corrected wording remain distinguishable. No action silently rewrites the claim or interprets the relationship selection as correct. No earlier Map revision is requested; this is a Design extension to its existing state rule.

RA4 — Make recovery consequences and handoff clearing inspectable.
Origin: Responsible AI specialist, refining the bounded recovery and reset specification at sequences 13 and 15.
Interaction: recovery preview shows the proposed wording and associated selections, including any change in representation or dissent. A restored agreement label remains a selected, unverified description; recovery is not fresh agreement. Cancel preserves current work; restoration consumes the snapshot. From the cover screen or working activity, handoff confirmation explains that clearing removes this group’s work and recovery. Cancel returns to the preceding screen with all work preserved. Confirm clears committed and original/corrected records, drafts, relationship selections, pairs, reveal progress, plans, practice, representation, dissent, previews, input values and activity-derived announcements. Clear retained application references and return to an empty opening state. Public fictional source material may remain.
Human reason: recovery must not conceal a change in whose explanation is represented, and the next group must not inherit prior working content. System reason: hiding fields or resetting the main object alone is insufficient if other application layers retain the activity.
Acceptance check: populate every layer with distinctive fictional markers. Cancel handoff and inspect preservation; then confirm from an edit, cover screen, recovery preview and practice state. Inspect controls, rendered content, announcements and recovery for marker absence. Recovery must be unavailable. Code and interaction review must also check the prohibition on network, persistent storage, telemetry and external assets. No check has been performed, and clearing is not device-wide privacy certification.

Tradeoffs and alternatives

The complete teacher-facilitated paper activity is a non-AI option and may be the preferred outcome. It must preserve the mission, exact A/B/C records, staged reveal, W/L prepared comparisons, claim/evidence relationship prompt, before/after positions, correction and separate dissent. Oral or scribed participation and passing remain possible. A facilitator can set aside or cover paper during an interruption, but paper handling also needs human agreement; it is not automatically confidential.

Retain the objections that C may feel like a trap, claim suggestions may cue responses, and an agreed-group record may conceal refusal. A generic dissent marker protects against requiring another text entry but does not identify every disputed contribution. Where the shared record cannot faithfully represent the discussion, pause synthesis and use oral or paper facilitation rather than manufacture agreement.

The new interruption screen offers immediate visibility control at the cost of another interaction. Preserving original wording supports accountable correction but can prolong exposure of superseded wording within the group. If these arrangements are unacceptable or infeasible, simplify the activity, choose paper-only delivery or reject the candidate.

Acceptance checks

The requirement checks above are proposed review procedures, not completed verification. Implemented behavior would need keyboard, focus, accessibility-presentation and state-transition inspection. Testing must cover combined states, including disagreement plus agreement, a pending edit inside an interruption, and handoff while a recovery preview exists.

Technical success would establish only the inspected behavior under the tested conditions. It would not establish confidentiality, voluntary agreement, belonging, learning or transfer. No real student records should be introduced to test these mechanisms.

Evidence and unknowns

The supplied basis consists of the seed and earlier draft sequences 4, 6, 8, 13, 15 and 20. No scenario or technical finding was supplied. The changes proposed here follow design inspection: interruption handling was unspecified, and sequence 20 adds state that must inherit correction and clearing rules. No observed incident or scenario-driven change is claimed.

Unknowns include device arrangements, interruption frequency, browser behavior, languages, support availability, lesson duration and whether learners can credibly refuse attribution. Apparent success could reflect imitation, adult cues or operator dominance. Apparent difficulty could reflect language barriers, time pressure, navigation or reasonable rejection of the task. Revision and completion cannot distinguish these explanations.

Practitioner review of science framing, facilitation and workload; student review of access, privacy expectations and credible dissent; and caregiver review of representation and shared-device boundaries all remain pending. So do technical checks, human pilot work and all field evidence about agency, dignity, access, sustainable workload, belonging, learning and transfer.

Next decision

Within Design, incorporate or explicitly reject RA1–RA4 in the orchestrator’s reviewable experience and paper package. Confirm that every adopted interaction is included in correction, recovery and handoff specifications before Build.
