This is an Implementation specialist expert draft for the Evidence Studio rehearsal, not an approved requirement or executed prototype. It addresses interaction design and executable prototyping, and behavioral verification and recovery. Its direct basis is hypothetical Scenario 27, Design revision 29 and revised Map 32. The parent iteration supplies background, not an approved baseline. No actual technical finding, participant observation, human authorization or measured outcome is supplied.

The coherent learner task is to help a fictional garden team explain what its records support: choose a claim and evidence pair, inspect descriptive differences, reveal C, select a prepared comparison and review a later position. The implementation challenge is preserving that focused journey while making correction, withdrawal, recovery and shared-device interruption reliable. A small artifact should mean a bounded task with inspectable behavior, not merely a short implementation that omits difficult state transitions.

Human and system capability

Human requirements: learners need intelligible evidence and authority over their wording and attribution requests. Passing, dissent, speech, another language and a scribe must remain available. Facilitators need a feasible process for contested removal and shared-device turns. Operating a control establishes neither authorship nor permission to remove someone else's contribution. Unresolved authority or scope calls for pausing the transaction and facilitated discussion.

System requirements: faithfully display supplied fictional records, preserve deliberate selections and keep committed work distinct from proposals. It must track application-created copies, support reviewed changes and enforce content-free withdrawal boundaries. It cannot authenticate permission, discover every paraphrase, evaluate arbitrary learner prose, verify group agreement or infer learning. No AI inference is needed.

Keep application activity in memory only. No network, persistent storage, telemetry, external assets, real student records, grades, rankings, disability inference or consequential scores are permitted. Application clearing is bounded removal of application-controlled content and references; it is not forensic erasure of browser or device memory.

Experience and decisions

Implement one progressively revealed studio. Start with the mission, A/B cards, a shared final-height scale and the opening claim decision. Offer suggestions, own wording and withhold with equal status. Confirm A/B honestly as the only available opening pair. The selected claim and exact comparison must appear together; the optional relationship describes the learner's view and may remain unanswered.

Reveal C only through learner action, with the neutral invitation that a position may be kept. Retain A/B and enable A/B, A/C and B/C. Pair selection updates recorded differences immediately without changing wording or relationship selections. Keep descriptive comparison changes distinct from committed edits to the learner's record.

The planning bench offers only the two supported choices. Changing the choice visibly switches the fixed W/L fixture, its conditions, heights and difference text together. Retain, narrow, revise and withhold open or update a proposal; they do not overwrite committed wording. Review exact proposed content before accepting it. The before/after synthesis remains correctable and visibly identifies withdrawal, incomplete history, representation and independent dissent.

Keep the two optional main-path wording controls, reused for correction. Do not add a withdrawal explanation field or a practice text field. Reveal scope review and recovery detail only when requested. Put status and browser limits in compact help; keep invented-data and interpretation limits next to evidence. Optional practice uses separate state and the other prepared fixture, with fewer suggestions and no claim of transfer.

Requirements and rationale

I1 — Use a single transaction boundary for authored records.
Origin: Systems engineer editing requirements carried into Design 29 and revised Map 32. Interaction: an edit constructs a proposal containing exact wording, pair, relationship, action, representation and dissent. A review renders that proposal. Confirm commits the reviewed proposal; cancel discards the ordinary edit without changing committed work. Correcting the initial position preserves distinguishable active versions. A later copy does not automatically update when its source is corrected.

Human reason: review must correspond to what will actually be represented. System reason: separate controls with independent mutation paths make cancellation and recovery inconsistent. Acceptance check: change wording and associated selections, inspect review, cancel, then repeat and confirm. The committed record must equal the reviewed proposal. Correct the initial wording while a later copy exists; the copy remains unchanged and retains its source dependency. All checks are proposed and unperformed.

Use a small explicit state vocabulary: committed activity, pending edit, recovery snapshot, withdrawal boundary and screen state. Committed activity includes initial versions, later position, comparison pair, reveal, plan, practice, representation and dissent. Each position or copied draft carries an internal contribution identifier and explicit dependency identifiers without participant identities. Screen state covers ordinary activity, proposal review, withdrawal review, recovery review, cover and handoff confirmation. Do not put recovery inside its own snapshot.

I2 — Make selective withdrawal a separate atomic operation.
Origin: Scenario 27, Design 29 and Map 32. Interaction: Withdraw initial position opens a scope review naming active versions, initial relationship and contribution-bound pair, tracked later copies, affected drafts and recovery consequences. Known dependent copies are included. Named controls let people include additional ambiguous later content or pause for facilitation; the system does not compare strings to infer ownership. Cancel preserves the previously suspended draft, preview and recovery exactly.

Human reason: correction and withholding do not satisfy a request to stop representing a contribution. System reason: partial removal permits stale copies to survive. Acceptance check: place different fictional markers in initial versions, a retain proposal, a corrected copy and an independent later position. Cancel withdrawal and inspect preservation. Confirm the reviewed scope and inspect removal of affected markers while independent work, planning, practice, representation and dissent remain.

Before confirmation, compute the proposed removal scope and recovery consequence without mutating activity. On confirmation, apply that same scope to committed records, pending proposals, recovery, input values, derived displays and announcements. Remove affected wording and versions; replace the initial slot with Initial position withdrawn. Clear its relationship and contribution-bound pair while preserving the independent current evidence comparison. Affected later positions become New position needed, lose wording and relationship, and retain their pair as comparison context. Remove any operative retain action referring to the withdrawn source.

Keep a content-free boundary outside ordinary recovery: the initial slot is closed for this group's activity, and reviewed affected contribution identifiers remain blocked from restoration. An explicit new independent later-position route creates a new contribution identifier and requires review; editing a copied draft does not remove its dependency. This records a selected route, not verified independence. Do not keep a hidden audit quotation, withdrawn reason or participation tally.

I3 — Make recovery subordinate to withdrawal.
Origin: the recovery exception required by Scenario 27 and specified in Design 29 and Map 32. Interaction: ordinary committed activity changes retain one preceding-state snapshot. Draft keystrokes, cover/resume and withdrawal do not create snapshots. Recovery review shows every consequential field and any removal limitation. Restore consumes the snapshot without creating reverse history; cancel preserves current work.

Human reason: repair should not reintroduce a contribution someone requested to withdraw. System reason: a snapshot predating removal may contain older versions or copies. Acceptance check: create recovery before initial correction, before a dependent retain commit and before a later independent change. Withdraw, then preview and restore available recovery. The initial slot remains withdrawn, affected copies cannot return, and unaffected fields recover together.

Sanitize the existing snapshot using the reviewed removal scope. If its remaining state is coherent, retain it with a disclosed reduced scope. If not, discard it and explain that recovery loss before withdrawal confirmation. Apply the boundary whenever snapshots are created, previewed or restored. Initial absence or older source versions in a snapshot must never reopen the withdrawn slot. Clear stale recovery previews after removal. Prefer an explicitly disclosed unavailable snapshot to a misleading partial restoration.

I4 — Separate interruption concealment from handoff.
Origin: Responsible AI interruption requirements incorporated into Design 29 and Map 32. Interaction: cover preserves activity and pending screens but removes working content from visible and accessibility presentation. Underlying controls cannot receive focus; activity-derived announcements stop. Resume returns to a usable control or heading without creating history. Handoff confirmation may be opened from activity or cover; cancellation returns to the preceding screen with work intact.

Human reason: interruptions should not require discarding work. System reason: concealment and reset have different persistence and focus behavior. Acceptance check: cover during an edit, withdrawal review and recovery preview, navigate by keyboard and resume. Confirm handoff from those same states and from practice. No prior marker, draft, dependency, withdrawal boundary, preview or recovery remains available through application controls.

Use genuinely hidden or inert underlying content with a focusable neutral cover screen, rather than a visual overlay alone. Avoid activity-derived accessible labels on cover controls. Handoff must clear the complete state inventory, rendered inputs, summaries, announcements and application-retained references, then construct a fresh empty opening state. Public fictional fixtures may remain. The brief help must say that cover is not a lock and clearing cannot control screenshots, browser history, autofill or device records.

I5 — Render exact sources through one comparison path.
Origin: source and planning requirements in Design 29 and revised Map 32, carrying the Systems engineer's authored fixtures and Learning scientist's descriptive comparison. Interaction: evidence cards, graphics, text equivalents and prepared comparisons derive from fixed public fixture data. Every bar uses a labeled 0–20 cm final-height scale with ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20. Selection states use words as well as styling.

Human reason: learners should not need visual inference or color recognition to compare records. System reason: separately maintained card, bar and description values can diverge. Acceptance check: inspect every fixture and switch every supported comparison. Values and descriptions must change together; arbitrary wording is displayed literally without execution or automatic judgment. Keep final height distinct from growth and leaves distinct from health.

Source checks: A is water 1 story unit/day, bright light, final height 12 cm, upright leaves. B is water 2, dim light, 18 cm, drooping leaves. C is water 2, bright light, 10 cm, upright leaves. All are an invented 14-day story. Starting height, type and soil remain unrecorded. A/B: B finishes 6 cm taller; water and light differ. A/C: A finishes 2 cm taller; light matches, water differs. B/C: B finishes 8 cm taller; water matches, light differs.

Hold light constant; compare water selects W1/W2: starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil mix S, bright light and 14 days match; water is 1/2, final heights are 11/13 cm, and both have upright leaves. W2 finishes 2 cm taller. Hold water constant; compare light selects L1/L2: starting height 4 cm, type T, soil mix S, water 2 and 14 days match; light is bright/dim, final heights are 9/14 cm and leaves upright/drooping. L2 finishes 5 cm taller. These are authored fixtures, not measurements or predictions. Temperature, individual variation, replication and allocation remain unspecified. They do not fill A/B/C gaps or establish causation.

Tradeoffs and alternatives

Selective removal increases complexity and can reduce recovery. A bounded snapshot keeps the promise inspectable, but later actions can replace earlier recovery. Suggested claims lower entry burden while cueing responses. Fixed fixtures expose planning consequences while restricting exploration. Retain the objections that C can feel like a trap, that polished summaries conceal refusal and that withdrawal removes useful history.

Scenario 27 changed the implementation requirement from mandatory retained originals and complete recoverable copies to active retention subject to reviewed withdrawal. Map 32 now closes the withdrawn initial slot and makes recovery subordinate to that boundary. Design 29 must incorporate those details before the candidate is treated as reconciled. This is an existing reconciliation dependency, not a newly observed defect or a request for another Map revision.

The complete teacher-facilitated paper activity is the non-AI alternative and may be preferred. Its distinct paper view must include the mission, exact A/B cards, a separate C reveal sheet, shared-scale graphics and text comparisons, W/L sheets with choice mapping, and before/after records. Include starting claim routes, optional relationships, all reconsideration actions, representation, independent dissent and separate optional practice. Include speech, another language, scribing, passing, correction review and one optional checkpoint. Withdrawal needs reviewed removal of affected lines, copies and checkpoint while preserving independent work; crossing out readable words is not removal. Paper handling and disposal require their own human arrangements.

Acceptance checks

Content and journey checks: exercise every starting claim route without required typing, reveal C, change all three pairs while preserving wording and relationship, switch W/L and return, and complete or skip practice. Inspect equal-status retain/narrow/revise/withhold, literal change feedback, selected but unverified agreement and independent dissent. No outcome may label correctness, causation, proficiency, health or learning.

State and failure checks: use fictional marker strings across active versions, drafts, copied proposals, independent work, previews and recovery. Exercise cancel and confirm from combined states, selective withdrawal, recovery before and after removal, cover/resume and handoff. Try an ordinary edit after withdrawal and verify that it cannot reopen the initial slot. Treat any resurfacing of a reviewed removed marker, silent wording replacement or cross-handoff recovery as a release-blocking technical failure for this candidate.

Access and fallback checks: complete the journey and removal by keyboard; inspect focus order, visible focus, announcements, concealed accessibility content, narrow layout and enlarged text. Inspect user wording containing markup-like characters for literal rendering. Review print styling and whether a teacher can facilitate the entire paper sequence from its materials alone. Human review of reading access, assistive-technology use and workload remains necessary.

Evidence and unknowns

Instrumentation should be limited to a compact, opt-in reviewer panel showing current screen, proposal type, recovery availability, withdrawal-boundary status and invariant failures. It must not duplicate learner wording or retain transition logs, removed content, hidden diagnostic snapshots or participation counts. It creates no telemetry, storage or network traffic. Fictional marker checks are reviewer procedures, not data collection from learners. An invariant display supports diagnosis but does not substitute for interaction and source review.

Useful invariants include a closed initial slot after withdrawal, no blocked dependency in restorable content, no operative retain source after removal, no underlying keyboard access while covered, and unavailable recovery after handoff. A failed invariant should stop the affected commit and preserve current work where possible, with a plain explanation and a route to cancel or facilitate. It must never silently substitute a claim or erase independent work as recovery from an error.

No implementation or checks have been executed in this turn. Intended quality includes inspectable decisions, faithful authorship, agency, dignity, access, belonging and manageable workload. Observed technical behavior is absent; learning, transfer and flourishing evidence remain pending. Unknowns include target devices and browsers, languages, assistance, interruption patterns, feasible lesson time and dependency-review workload. Apparent success could reflect suggestions, adult cues, imitation or fixture familiarity. Difficulty could reflect language access, navigation, group control, time pressure or reasonable rejection of the framing.

Next decision

This is the Learning engineer’s orchestrated Design revision brief for a lifecycle rehearsal. Its basis is the domain contributor at sequence 4, Human-centered designer at 6, Understand synthesis at 8, Systems engineer at 13, provisional Map at 15, Learning scientist at 20, Responsible AI specialist at 22, Design synthesis at 24 and hypothetical scenario at 27. These are project drafts, not participant evidence or approved requirements. The parent school-science iteration is background only.

Middle-school learners help a fictional school garden team explain what its records support. Teachers and classroom support staff would facilitate; caregivers are affected-person reviewers. None has participated. A reasoning deficit has not been established. Difficulty could reflect language, unfamiliar units, navigation, time pressure, operator dominance or rejection of the framing. Apparent success could reflect suggestions, imitation, adult cues or fixture familiarity.

Sequence 27 hypothesizes a learner requesting removal of their initial wording while preserving other work. Correction retains originals, withholding retains history, covering allows resumption and handoff clears the whole group. These do not meet that request. Map sequence 15 explicitly requires retained originals and whole-state recovery, so Map is the earliest artifact requiring revision. Understand already permits contesting attribution; the fictional inquiry framing remains usable.

Human and system capability

Human requirements: learners need time, intelligible evidence and control over wording and attribution. Speech, another language, a scribe, passing and dissent remain available. Withdrawal must require neither personal identification nor a reason. Facilitators need feasible discussion and language support, flexible device turns and a way to pause contested authorship or removal. Operating controls does not establish authority to speak for others or remove their work.

System requirements: display exact records and descriptive differences; preserve deliberate choices; distinguish correction, withholding, withdrawal, covering and handoff. Use explicit proposal review, cancellation and one bounded recovery snapshot. Add source-dependency bookkeeping for application-created copies without inferring authorship or semantic equivalence. No AI inference is needed. No real student records, automated grades, rankings, disability inference or consequential scores are permitted. Use no network, storage, telemetry or external assets.

Science practitioners and teachers would review framing, fixtures, paper completeness and workload. Students would review comprehension, access, credible passing, dissent and withdrawal. Caregivers would review representation and shared-device expectations. These proposed responsibilities are unaccepted; all review remains pending. Separate assessment stays outside the candidate.

Experience and decisions

Open with: “Help the fictional garden team explain what its records support. Compare two records, offer a claim, then decide what another record changes.” Show A/B, a shared final-height graphic and one claim decision. Keep fictional labels and interpretation limits beside evidence. Put facilitation, paper materials and review status in compact help.

Offer equally presented starting suggestions: “B finishes taller than A in these records”; “Water-2 plants always finish taller in this story”; “These records do not settle what caused the height difference”; own wording; or withhold. Confirm A/B honestly as the only available pair. Beside the claim show the descriptive comparison. Optional relationship choices are “My claim describes these records,” “My claim goes beyond these records,” and “I have not decided how they connect.” Label these as learner-selected views; leaving them unanswered does not block progress.

Introduce C neutrally: “Another fictional record may complicate the explanation. You can keep your position.” Learner-triggered reveal retains earlier cards and enables A/B, A/C and B/C selection. Pair changes update recorded differences while preserving wording and the selected relationship, with a neutral invitation to reconsider.

At the planning bench, choosing which recorded condition to hold constant displays fixed W or L records. This selects a prepared example, not an experiment or prediction. Then offer retain, narrow, revise and withhold at equal status. An action labels a proposal; it does not silently rewrite committed wording. Review exact wording, pair, relationship, action, representation and dissent before confirmation. Cancel preserves committed work.

The synthesis shows initial and later positions with literal change descriptions. Default representation to one offered explanation. Agreement and unresolved discussion require deliberate selection; agreement remains unverified. Keep an independent dissent marker. Passing preserves work without a tally or inferred agreement.

Add a named “Withdraw initial position” action beside its correction control. Review the removal scope and dependent consequences before confirmation. A withdrawn position becomes a content-free label, not a retained quotation. Dependent later wording needs a new deliberate choice; independent later work remains. Where removal authority or dependency is contested, pause and facilitate rather than certify permission through a click.

Optional supported practice uses the other W/L fixture, fewer suggestions and separate state. Offer its final-height observation, withhold or an oral own-position route, plus optional relationship and retain/revise/withhold controls. No third text field is needed. It is skippable and cannot establish retention or transfer.

Requirements and rationale

R1 — Focused evidence and faithful sources. Origins: domain sequence 4, Human-centered designer 6, Understand 8 and Map 15. Use at most two optional main-path text controls, initial and later wording, reused for correction. No typing is required. Final-height graphics share a labeled 0–20 cm scale with ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20, exact numeric values and text equivalents. Conditions and selection states use words, not color alone. Reason: reading stamina, typing and visual inference should not become hidden prerequisites. Check all values, pair descriptions and text equivalents; no height-as-growth or leaves-as-health labels may appear.

R2 — Inspectable claim scope and neutral reconsideration. Origins: Learning scientist 20, extending domain 4, Human-centered designer 6 and Map 15. Place claim, selected pair, exact comparison and optional relationship together. Pair changes preserve interpretation selections. Retain proposes current initial wording; narrow/revise require explicit suggestion selection or later own wording; withhold proposes no current claim while preserving history unless separately withdrawn. Reason: choices support examination without interpreting arbitrary prose or rewarding compliance. Check every route, own wording, unanswered relationships and retained wording with a changed pair. Feedback describes changes, never improvement or demonstrated understanding.

R3 — Fixed planning and bounded practice. Origins: Systems engineer 13, Map 15 and Learning scientist 20. “Hold light constant; compare water” selects W1/W2. “Hold water constant; compare light” selects L1/L2. Show matching/differing records, final-height differences and unknowns together. Keep optional practice separate from A/B/C. Reason: planning needs visible consequences without an unsupported calculator. Check W/L switching and exact restoration, unchanged A/B/C, skippable practice and no transfer claim.

R4 — Contestable representation. Origins: Human-centered designer 6, Systems engineer 13 and Responsible AI specialist 22. Agreement plus dissent preserves both selections and displays a neutral representation-review notice. Passing changes no contribution. Reason: recording selections cannot establish consensus or equitable participation. Check the combined state and deliberate correction without automatic attribution changes. Social credibility remains a human-review question.

R5 — Correction, withdrawal and dependency boundaries. Origins: Systems engineer 13, Map 15 and Responsible AI specialist 22; revised in response to Scenario 27 and Design 24. Ordinary correction preserves identifiable original wording only while that contribution remains active. Withdrawal is a separate reviewed transaction. Its preview identifies the selected initial contribution, all versions, associated relationship, application-created copies and affected later proposals. Cancel preserves committed state, drafts and recovery exactly.

On confirmation, remove that contribution’s wording and versions from records, inputs, drafts, previews, announcements and derived summaries. Clear its associated initial interpretation and replace its displayed position with “Initial position withdrawn.” Keep public fictional evidence, independent later contributions, planning, practice and dissent. A later retain copy or dependent proposal loses copied wording and shows “New position needed”; do not substitute another claim. Preserve independent representation selections as unverified descriptions, with a notice that the synthesis is now incomplete.

Track application-created dependencies through copying, correction and proposals. For ambiguous manually entered copies, the review must let people identify affected content or pause for facilitation; the system must not infer ownership from matching strings. Removal guarantees must be limited to the reviewed contribution and identified copies. It cannot discover every paraphrase or authenticate permission.

Reason: authorship includes contesting continued representation, while independent work also deserves preservation. Check cancellation, marker removal from every affected layer, dependency invalidation, preserved independent content and keyboard operation without another text field. Confirming scope is not proof of human authorization. Map must settle this revised authority and dependency boundary before Build.

R6 — Recovery, interruption and handoff. Origins: Systems engineer 13, Map 15, Responsible AI specialist 22; withdrawal exception from Scenario 27. Ordinary committed changes retain one preceding-state snapshot, including wording versions, pairs, relationships, actions, reveal, plan, practice, representation and dissent. Draft keystrokes create no history. Preview all consequential fields; cancel preserves current state; restoration consumes the snapshot without creating reverse history.

Withdrawal must not create a snapshot containing removed content. Sanitize affected records and dependent copies in the existing snapshot before it can be previewed or restored. Maintain a content-free withdrawal boundary outside ordinary undo so recovery cannot resurrect the withdrawn initial contribution. If sanitization cannot preserve a coherent snapshot, discard it and explain the lost recovery before confirmation. Later recovery remains subject to that boundary; handoff clears it. Check restoration after withdrawal, including a snapshot predating correction or a dependent retain proposal.

Cover activity removes work from visible and accessibility presentation, prevents underlying focus and suppresses activity-derived announcements. Preserve committed state, drafts and previews; cover/resume creates no snapshot. Focus enters a neutral screen and returns to a usable control or heading. Cover is not a lock: anyone can resume.

Confirmed handoff clears records, versions, drafts, dependencies, withdrawal boundary, relationships, pairs, actions, representation, dissent, reveal, plan, practice, previews, recovery, input values, announcements and retained application references. Cancel returns to the preceding activity, cover or preview with work intact. Brief help explains limits concerning screenshots, browser history, autofill and device records. Check all layers with fictional markers; recovery cannot cross handoff.

R7 — Access and complete paper delivery. Origins: domain 4, Human-centered designer 6, Systems engineer 13, Learning scientist 20, Responsible AI specialist 22 and Scenario 27. Use native named controls, visible focus, predictable keyboard order, readable responsive layout and accessible update notifications without unexpected focus movement. Every graphic has a full text equivalent. Reason: browser access is only one participation condition. Check keyboard completion, enlarged text, narrow layout and assistive-technology presentation. The standalone paper package below must support the same decisions; paper-equivalence and preparation workload remain untested.

Standalone source and paper package

All cards are an invented 14-day story, not measurements, plant-care advice or real outcomes. Opening A: water 1 story unit/day; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves. B: water 2 story units/day; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves. Separately revealed C: water 2 story units/day; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves. Starting height, plant type and soil are unrecorded. Final height is not growth; leaves do not establish health.

Draw labeled bars on the shared 0–20 cm scale. Full text comparisons: A/B — B finishes 6 cm taller; water and light differ. A/C — A finishes 2 cm taller; light matches and water differs. B/C — B finishes 8 cm taller; water matches and light differs. Unknown conditions remain unknown. C challenges the universal water-2 claim without establishing an opposite causal rule.

Prepared W sheet: W1/W2 both record starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil S, bright light and 14 days. W1: water 1 story unit/day, final height 11 cm, upright leaves. W2: water 2, final height 13 cm, upright leaves. Water differs; other listed conditions match; W2 finishes 2 cm taller. Select W for holding light constant and comparing water.

Prepared L sheet: L1/L2 both record starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil S, water 2 story units/day and 14 days. L1: bright light, final height 9 cm, upright leaves. L2: dim light, final height 14 cm, drooping leaves. Light differs; other listed conditions match; L2 finishes 5 cm taller. Select L for holding water constant and comparing light.

Use the same bar scale and text equivalents for W/L. These additional authored fixtures originate at sequence 13 and do not fill A/B/C gaps. Temperature, individual variation and other conditions are unrecorded; replication and allocation are unspecified. Fixed outcomes establish neither causes nor predictions.

Facilitator sequence: present mission and A/B; offer the opening claim choices, own wording or withhold; confirm A/B and optionally discuss the relationship. Ask, “What do these records say, and what does your claim add?” Introduce C without requiring change; let learners choose any pair. Offer the two planning choices and corresponding sheet, then review the later position. Optionally use the other fixture as supported practice. Additional proposed controls can be discussed without fabricated outcomes.

Paper record: initial claim/withhold and pair A/B; optional relationship; original and explicitly corrected wording while active. Later record: retain/narrow/revise/withhold, exact position, selected pair and optional relationship. Representation: one offered explanation/agreed group explanation/unresolved discussion; separate dissent present/not marked. Agreement is selected, not verified. Optional practice has a separate fixture, position, relationship and reconsideration record.

Allow speech, another language, a scribe and passing. Review corrections separately and accept or cancel. Keep at most one agreed paper checkpoint for optional recovery. For withdrawal, review selected lines, dependent copies and checkpoint; remove affected content by human agreement while preserving independent work. Dependent positions need a new choice. Ordinary crossing-out leaves words readable and must not be presented as removal. Paper handling, replacement sheets, copies and disposal need an agreed routine; browser clearing cannot control them. Cover or set aside papers during interruption. Build should include a distinct paper view with usable print styling; no participant names are needed.

Tradeoffs and alternatives

Retain objections that C can feel like a trap, suggestions can constrain interpretation, a polished synthesis can conceal refusal and withdrawal can remove useful reasoning history. Neutral reveal and explicit representation are proposed responses, not demonstrated resolutions. Sequence 27 changes mandatory retention into retention subject to reviewed withdrawal, and makes recovery subordinate to removal boundaries.

Selective removal adds complexity and possible misuse. When attribution or dependencies cannot be resolved, pause synthesis and use facilitated oral or paper discussion. Complete teacher-facilitated paper delivery is the non-AI alternative and may be preferred. Simplifying language, changing device arrangements, reducing scope, replacing fixtures or rejecting the candidate remain legitimate.

Acceptance checks

Content and decisions: inspect every source value and scale; exercise every claim, pair, relationship and reconsideration route without required typing. Switch W/L and skip or revisit separate practice. Verify descriptive feedback without grades, causal endorsement, health inference or learning claims.

State and removal: use fictional markers in original wording, correction, dependent later proposals, drafts and recovery. Cancel withdrawal and inspect exact preservation; confirm and inspect affected layers for absence. Restore sanitized recovery and verify no resurrection. Check independent work and dissent, new-choice prompts, ordinary cancellation/correction, cover/resume and full handoff from combined states.

Access and paper: complete the journey and withdrawal by keyboard; inspect focus, announcements, concealed accessibility content, narrow layout and enlarged text. A teacher reviewer should be able to facilitate the complete paper sequence, including removal and disagreement, from its materials alone. All checks are proposed and unperformed.

Evidence and unknowns

Intended quality includes meaningful inquiry, faithful authorship, agency, dignity, access, belonging and manageable workload. Observed technical behavior is absent. Technical verification would establish only inspected behavior, not voluntary agreement, classroom suitability, learning, retention, transfer or flourishing.

The hypothetical removal request could reflect misattribution, discomfort, changed interpretation or rejection of shared recording. It establishes neither coercion nor misunderstanding. Languages, devices, browsers, time, interruption frequency, staffing, printing and feasible dependency review remain unknown. Practitioner and affected-person review, human pilots and all field evidence remain pending. Later learning inquiry must separate supported performance from delayed retention and changed-context performance, document assistance and rival explanations, and retain access supports.

Next decision

Request one revision of Map’s retention, dependency, authority and recovery requirements using sequence 27. Hold Build while that boundary remains unresolved, then reconcile this Design brief with the revised Map. No Understand revision is requested. This is the Learning engineer’s orchestrated Map revision for a lifecycle rehearsal. It integrates domain sequence 4, Human-centered designer 6, Understand synthesis 8, Systems engineer 13, Map synthesis 15, Learning scientist 20, Responsible AI specialist 22, Design synthesis 24, hypothetical scenario 27 and Design revision 29. These are project drafts and authored examples, not participant observations, approved requirements or demonstrated expertise. The parent iteration remains background only.

Sequence 27 hypothesizes a learner asking to remove their initial wording while leaving other work. Map 15 requires identifiable originals and whole-state recovery; correction, withholding, covering and handoff cannot satisfy that selective request. This revision replaces those retention and recovery boundaries. Understand 8 already permits contested attribution, so no revision of Understand is requested. Design 29 supplies a proposed response; Map now specifies its dependencies and limits before Design reconciliation and Build.

Problem, people and rival explanations

Middle-school learners help a fictional school garden team explain what its records support. Teachers and support staff would facilitate; caregivers are affected-person reviewers. None has participated. The meaningful decisions concern claim scope, evidence selection, reconsideration and selecting a prepared comparison. A reasoning deficit has not been established.

Difficulty could reflect language access, unfamiliar units, navigation, time pressure, unequal device control or rejection of the framing. Apparent success could reflect suggested answers, imitation, adult cues or fixture familiarity. The hypothetical withdrawal request could reflect misattribution, discomfort, changed interpretation or rejection of shared recording. It establishes neither coercion nor misunderstanding. Revision, retention, withdrawal and completion are not competence measures.

Human capability, authority and support

Learners need intelligible evidence, discussion time and control over wording and attribution. Oral responses, another language, a scribe, passing and dissent must remain available. Withdrawal requires neither an identity nor a reason. Device operation confers no authority to speak for everyone or remove another contribution.

Facilitators need a feasible routine for language support, flexible device turns and pausing contested authorship or removal. A pause preserves work; it does not certify permission or decide the science claim. When people cannot resolve removal scope, stop the transaction and use facilitated oral or paper discussion. Do not offer a control that claims to verify consent. Any separate assessment remains outside the candidate.

Proposed practitioner review covers science framing, fixtures, paper completeness and workload. Proposed student review covers comprehension, access, credible passing, dissent and withdrawal. Proposed caregiver review covers representation and shared-device expectations. These responsibilities are unaccepted; review, human pilots and real-use decisions remain pending.

System capability and limits

The system displays fictional records, descriptive differences and deliberate selections. No AI inference is needed. It cannot authenticate authorship, establish agreement, detect coercion, discover every paraphrase or infer learning. No real student records, grades, rankings, disability inference or consequential scores are permitted.

Use only in-memory activity state: no network, storage, telemetry or external assets. Provide keyboard operation, named selection states, visible focus, readable responsive layout and full text equivalents. Keep review metadata in compact help and fictional labels beside evidence. Technical clearing concerns application-controlled state, not forensic erasure of browser or device memory.

Source specification and planning dependencies

A/B/C are an invented 14-day story, not measurements, plant-care advice or real outcomes. A: water 1 story unit/day; bright light; final height 12 cm; upright leaves. B: water 2; dim light; final height 18 cm; drooping leaves. C: water 2; bright light; final height 10 cm; upright leaves. Starting height, plant type and soil are unrecorded. Final height is not growth; leaves do not establish health.

A/B: B finishes 6 cm taller; water and light differ. A/C: A finishes 2 cm taller; light matches and water differs. B/C: B finishes 8 cm taller; water matches and light differs. Unknowns remain unknown. C challenges the universal descriptive water-2 claim without establishing an opposite causal rule.

Prepared W, authored at Systems engineer sequence 13: W1/W2 both record starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil mix S, bright light and 14 days. W1 records water 1 story unit/day, final height 11 cm, upright leaves. W2 records water 2, final height 13 cm, upright leaves. Water differs; other listed conditions match; W2 finishes 2 cm taller. Select W for “Hold light constant; compare water.”

Prepared L, also authored at sequence 13: L1/L2 both record starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil mix S, water 2 story units/day and 14 days. L1 records bright light, final height 9 cm, upright leaves. L2 records dim light, final height 14 cm, drooping leaves. Light differs; other listed conditions match; L2 finishes 5 cm taller. Select L for “Hold water constant; compare light.”

W/L are separate authored fictional examples and do not fill A/B/C gaps. Temperature, individual variation and other conditions are unrecorded; replication and allocation are unspecified. Fixed outcomes establish neither causes nor predictions. Practitioners may replace or reject the fixtures.

Coupled requirements and observable checks

R1 — Inspectable inquiry with low entry burden. Origins: domain 4, Human-centered designer 6, Understand 8 and Map 15. Open with a short mission to help the fictional team explain its records. Begin with A/B, a claim choice and honest confirmation of the only available pair. Offer a bounded observation, a broader claim to investigate, causal uncertainty, own wording and withhold without a preferred-answer hierarchy. Use at most two optional main-path text controls, initial and later wording, reused for correction. No typing is required.

Reason: reading stamina, typing and visual inference must not become hidden prerequisites. Use final-height graphics on a labeled 0–20 cm scale with ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20, numeric values and text equivalents. Check all values, selection names and interpretation limits; complete the opening without typing. All checks are proposed, not performed.

R2 — Comparison, practice and faithful reconsideration. Origins: domain 4, Human-centered designer 6, Systems engineer 13 and Learning scientist 20. Show the selected claim beside the selected pair, exact recorded differences and unknowns. Optional relationship choices describe the learner’s view: describes these records, goes beyond these records, or connection undecided. Leaving this unanswered cannot block progress. Pair changes update descriptive facts while preserving wording and the selected relationship.

Introduce C neutrally and reveal it through learner action; keep earlier records accessible and enable A/B, A/C and B/C. Offer retain, narrow, revise and withhold equally. Retain proposes current active initial wording; narrow/revise require deliberate wording selection or entry; withhold records no current claim while preserving active history. Review proposals before confirmation. Feedback describes literal changes, never improvement or demonstrated understanding.

Reason: meaningful practice requires visible consequences and permission to keep a position. Check all routes, own wording, unanswered relationships, retain with a changed pair and cancellation. Switch W/L and back; verify corresponding records and text together without changing A/B/C. Optional practice uses the other fixture, fewer suggestions and separate state without a third text field. It is skippable supported practice, not retention or transfer evidence.

R3 — Contestable representation. Origins: Human-centered designer 6, Systems engineer 13 and Responsible AI specialist 22. Default to one offered explanation. Agreement and unresolved discussion require deliberate selection; label agreement as selected and unverified. Dissent remains independent of scientific revision. Agreement plus dissent preserves both selections and displays a neutral review notice. Passing changes no contribution and creates no tally.

Reason: selection authority is narrower than authority to represent people. Check the combined agreement/dissent state, deliberate correction and passing. Credible refusal and equitable participation require human review; controls cannot establish them.

R4 — Ordinary correction and contribution dependencies. Origins: Systems engineer 13 and Map 15, extended by Learning scientist 20, Responsible AI specialist 22 and Scenario 27. Separate committed records, pending proposals and one preceding-state recovery snapshot. Confirm commits exactly the reviewed proposal. Ordinary edit cancellation discards that proposal and preserves committed work. Original and corrected wording remain identifiable only while the contribution remains active.

Assign internal contribution and version identifiers without identities. Application-created copies, including retain proposals, carry explicit source dependencies through drafts, committed records and recovery. Editing a copied proposal does not silently remove that dependency. A new independent later position requires a deliberate new-position route and review; the system records the selected route, not verified independence. Correcting the initial position does not silently update an existing later copy.

Reason: copied wording can outlive its source unless the dependency is represented. Check correction followed by retain, editing a retain draft and creating an independent later proposal. Inspect exact wording and dependency scope; no automatic attribution or semantic inference is permitted.

R5 — Reviewed selective withdrawal. Origins: Scenario 27, addressing Map 15 and Design 24; developed in Design revision 29. Provide “Withdraw initial position” separately from correction, withholding and handoff. Its preview identifies the initial contribution, versions, initial interpretation, tracked copies, affected proposals and recovery consequence. Offer confirm, cancel and pause for facilitation without another text field. Cancellation preserves committed work, existing drafts, previews and recovery exactly.

Known dependent copies are included in removal. For manually entered or otherwise ambiguous content, provide named controls to identify additional affected later content or pause. Do not match strings or infer ownership. Preview all consequences before confirmation. Scope guarantees cover the reviewed contribution, tracked copies and explicitly identified content; the system cannot promise to discover every paraphrase.

Confirmation removes affected wording and versions from records, controls, drafts, previews, announcements and derived displays. Replace the initial position with a content-free “Initial position withdrawn” marker and clear its associated interpretation and contribution-bound pair. Keep the public evidence and independent current comparison. A dependent later position loses its wording and associated interpretation, becomes “New position needed,” and requires a new deliberate action; preserve its evidence pair as comparison context. Do not substitute a claim or leave an operative retain action referring to removed wording.

Preserve independent later work, planning, practice, representation and dissent unless explicitly included in the reviewed scope. Representation remains unverified, and the synthesis states that its history is incomplete. The withdrawn initial slot cannot be restored or silently refilled during this group’s activity; new independent later work remains possible. Record no identity, reason or participation tally.

Reason: control over continued representation can require removal while independent work deserves preservation. Check cancellation and confirmation with distinct fictional markers in originals, corrections, copied proposals, drafts and summaries. Verify affected content is absent, independent content and dissent remain, and new choices are required. Confirmation does not establish human authorization.

R6 — Recovery subordinate to withdrawal. Origins: Systems engineer 13, Map 15 and Responsible AI specialist 22; exception required by Scenario 27 and Design revision 29. Ordinary committed changes keep one nonrecursive preceding-state snapshot covering wording versions, pairs, relationships, actions, reveal, planning, practice, representation and dissent. Draft keystrokes create no history. Preview consequential fields; cancel preserves current work; restore consumes the snapshot without creating reverse history.

Withdrawal creates no snapshot of removed content. Before confirmation, determine whether the existing snapshot can be sanitized coherently and disclose whether recovery will be reduced or discarded. On confirmation, sanitize its affected versions and dependencies with the same removal rules or discard it. Remove any stale recovery preview. Keep a content-free withdrawal boundary outside ordinary snapshots. Apply that boundary when creating, previewing or restoring later snapshots, so recovery cannot restore the withdrawn initial slot or identified copies.

Reason: undo must not defeat a deliberate withdrawal. Check recovery predating an initial correction, a dependent retain proposal and a later independent change. Restore sanitized recovery and inspect all affected layers for absence; verify preserved independent fields and disclosed recovery loss. Implementation must pass these checks before any human pilot is considered.

R7 — Interruption and complete handoff. Origins: Systems engineer 13, Responsible AI specialist 22, Scenario 27 and Design revision 29. Cover activity removes working content from visible and accessibility presentation, prevents underlying focus and suppresses activity-derived announcements. Preserve work and pending screens exactly; covering/resuming creates no snapshot. Focus enters a neutral screen and returns to a usable control or heading. Cover is not a lock; anyone can resume.

Confirmed handoff clears records, versions, drafts, dependencies, withdrawal boundaries, pairs, relationships, actions, representation, dissent, reveal, planning, practice, previews, recovery, input values, announcements and retained application references. Return to an empty opening state. Cancel returns to the prior activity, cover or preview with work intact. Public fictional sources may remain. Recovery cannot cross handoff.

Reason: concealment, selective withdrawal and group reset have different purposes. Check cover/resume and handoff from edits, withdrawal previews, recovery and practice. Use fictional markers across all layers. Brief help explains screenshots, browser history, autofill and other device limits without displacing the mission.

Access and complete non-AI delivery

Origins: domain 4, Human-centered designer 6, Systems engineer 13, Learning scientist 20, Responsible AI specialist 22 and Scenario 27. Every decision, including withdrawal and scope review, needs native named controls, keyboard operation, clear focus and predictable order. Updates need accessible notifications without unexpected focus movement. Check narrow layout, enlarged text, text equivalents and assistive-technology presentation. These checks remain unperformed.

The complete teacher-facilitated paper alternative must contain the mission, exact A/B cards, separately revealed C, shared-scale graphics and every text comparison above, W/L sheets with their choice mapping, and a before/after record. Include all starting claim routes, optional relationship responses, retain/narrow/revise/withhold, selected pairs, representation and independent dissent. Optional practice has a separate record. Teachers must not reconstruct the sequence from browser controls.

Facilitate A/B and a claim first; ask neutrally what the records say and what the claim adds. Reveal C without requiring revision, choose a pair, select W/L, review the later position, then optionally use the other fixture. Allow speech, another language, a scribe and passing. Review corrections separately and accept or cancel. Retain at most one agreed paper checkpoint for optional recovery.

For paper withdrawal, review affected lines, copies and checkpoint by human agreement; replace affected sheets or use an agreed removal routine while preserving independent work. Crossing out readable words is not removal. Dependent positions need a new choice. Cover or set aside papers during interruption. Handling, copies and disposal require their own arrangements; browser clearing cannot control them. Check that a teacher reviewer can facilitate the entire sequence, including dissent and withdrawal, using the materials alone. Paper-only delivery is a legitimate preferred outcome.

Tradeoffs, dissent and evidence

Retain objections that C can feel like a trap, suggestions constrain interpretation, polished synthesis conceals refusal and withdrawal removes useful history. Neutral reveal, explicit representation and selective removal are proposed responses, not demonstrated resolutions. Selective removal also creates misuse and workload risks. Unresolved attribution, unavailable support or incoherent removal scope justify pausing, simplifying, choosing paper or rejecting the candidate.

Intended quality includes agency, dignity, access, belonging, sustainable workload and opportunities for learning. Observed technical behavior is absent. Technical verification would establish only inspected implementation behavior, not voluntary agreement, privacy beyond the application, classroom suitability or learning.

Languages, reading supports, devices, browsers, time, interruption frequency, staffing, printing and feasible dependency review remain unknown. All practitioner and affected-person review, human pilots and field evidence remain pending. Future learning inquiry must distinguish supported performance, delayed retention and changed-context performance, document assistance and rival explanations, and retain access supports.

Next decision

Use this revised Map as the provisional authority and state specification. Return to Design reconciliation of sequence 29 before Build, carrying these boundaries into its complete brief and paper package. This completes the requested Map revision; no additional earlier-stage revisit is requested. Technical verification, human review, fixture replacement, paper-only delivery and rejection remain open. This is an Implementation specialist expert draft for the Evidence Studio rehearsal, not an approved requirement or executed prototype. It addresses interaction design and executable prototyping, and behavioral verification and recovery. Its direct basis is hypothetical Scenario 27, Design revision 29 and revised Map 32. The parent iteration supplies background, not an approved baseline. No actual technical finding, participant observation, human authorization or measured outcome is supplied.

The coherent learner task is to help a fictional garden team explain what its records support: choose a claim and evidence pair, inspect descriptive differences, reveal C, select a prepared comparison and review a later position. The implementation challenge is preserving that focused journey while making correction, withdrawal, recovery and shared-device interruption reliable. A small artifact should mean a bounded task with inspectable behavior, not merely a short implementation that omits difficult state transitions.

Human and system capability

Human requirements: learners need intelligible evidence and authority over their wording and attribution requests. Passing, dissent, speech, another language and a scribe must remain available. Facilitators need a feasible process for contested removal and shared-device turns. Operating a control establishes neither authorship nor permission to remove someone else's contribution. Unresolved authority or scope calls for pausing the transaction and facilitated discussion.

System requirements: faithfully display supplied fictional records, preserve deliberate selections and keep committed work distinct from proposals. It must track application-created copies, support reviewed changes and enforce content-free withdrawal boundaries. It cannot authenticate permission, discover every paraphrase, evaluate arbitrary learner prose, verify group agreement or infer learning. No AI inference is needed.

Keep application activity in memory only. No network, persistent storage, telemetry, external assets, real student records, grades, rankings, disability inference or consequential scores are permitted. Application clearing is bounded removal of application-controlled content and references; it is not forensic erasure of browser or device memory.

Experience and decisions

Implement one progressively revealed studio. Start with the mission, A/B cards, a shared final-height scale and the opening claim decision. Offer suggestions, own wording and withhold with equal status. Confirm A/B honestly as the only available opening pair. The selected claim and exact comparison must appear together; the optional relationship describes the learner's view and may remain unanswered.

Reveal C only through learner action, with the neutral invitation that a position may be kept. Retain A/B and enable A/B, A/C and B/C. Pair selection updates recorded differences immediately without changing wording or relationship selections. Keep descriptive comparison changes distinct from committed edits to the learner's record.

The planning bench offers only the two supported choices. Changing the choice visibly switches the fixed W/L fixture, its conditions, heights and difference text together. Retain, narrow, revise and withhold open or update a proposal; they do not overwrite committed wording. Review exact proposed content before accepting it. The before/after synthesis remains correctable and visibly identifies withdrawal, incomplete history, representation and independent dissent.

Keep the two optional main-path wording controls, reused for correction. Do not add a withdrawal explanation field or a practice text field. Reveal scope review and recovery detail only when requested. Put status and browser limits in compact help; keep invented-data and interpretation limits next to evidence. Optional practice uses separate state and the other prepared fixture, with fewer suggestions and no claim of transfer.

Requirements and rationale

I1 — Use a single transaction boundary for authored records.
Origin: Systems engineer editing requirements carried into Design 29 and revised Map 32. Interaction: an edit constructs a proposal containing exact wording, pair, relationship, action, representation and dissent. A review renders that proposal. Confirm commits the reviewed proposal; cancel discards the ordinary edit without changing committed work. Correcting the initial position preserves distinguishable active versions. A later copy does not automatically update when its source is corrected.

Human reason: review must correspond to what will actually be represented. System reason: separate controls with independent mutation paths make cancellation and recovery inconsistent. Acceptance check: change wording and associated selections, inspect review, cancel, then repeat and confirm. The committed record must equal the reviewed proposal. Correct the initial wording while a later copy exists; the copy remains unchanged and retains its source dependency. All checks are proposed and unperformed.

Use a small explicit state vocabulary: committed activity, pending edit, recovery snapshot, withdrawal boundary and screen state. Committed activity includes initial versions, later position, comparison pair, reveal, plan, practice, representation and dissent. Each position or copied draft carries an internal contribution identifier and explicit dependency identifiers without participant identities. Screen state covers ordinary activity, proposal review, withdrawal review, recovery review, cover and handoff confirmation. Do not put recovery inside its own snapshot.

I2 — Make selective withdrawal a separate atomic operation.
Origin: Scenario 27, Design 29 and Map 32. Interaction: Withdraw initial position opens a scope review naming active versions, initial relationship and contribution-bound pair, tracked later copies, affected drafts and recovery consequences. Known dependent copies are included. Named controls let people include additional ambiguous later content or pause for facilitation; the system does not compare strings to infer ownership. Cancel preserves the previously suspended draft, preview and recovery exactly.

Human reason: correction and withholding do not satisfy a request to stop representing a contribution. System reason: partial removal permits stale copies to survive. Acceptance check: place different fictional markers in initial versions, a retain proposal, a corrected copy and an independent later position. Cancel withdrawal and inspect preservation. Confirm the reviewed scope and inspect removal of affected markers while independent work, planning, practice, representation and dissent remain.

Before confirmation, compute the proposed removal scope and recovery consequence without mutating activity. On confirmation, apply that same scope to committed records, pending proposals, recovery, input values, derived displays and announcements. Remove affected wording and versions; replace the initial slot with Initial position withdrawn. Clear its relationship and contribution-bound pair while preserving the independent current evidence comparison. Affected later positions become New position needed, lose wording and relationship, and retain their pair as comparison context. Remove any operative retain action referring to the withdrawn source.

Keep a content-free boundary outside ordinary recovery: the initial slot is closed for this group's activity, and reviewed affected contribution identifiers remain blocked from restoration. An explicit new independent later-position route creates a new contribution identifier and requires review; editing a copied draft does not remove its dependency. This records a selected route, not verified independence. Do not keep a hidden audit quotation, withdrawn reason or participation tally.

I3 — Make recovery subordinate to withdrawal.
Origin: the recovery exception required by Scenario 27 and specified in Design 29 and Map 32. Interaction: ordinary committed activity changes retain one preceding-state snapshot. Draft keystrokes, cover/resume and withdrawal do not create snapshots. Recovery review shows every consequential field and any removal limitation. Restore consumes the snapshot without creating reverse history; cancel preserves current work.

Human reason: repair should not reintroduce a contribution someone requested to withdraw. System reason: a snapshot predating removal may contain older versions or copies. Acceptance check: create recovery before initial correction, before a dependent retain commit and before a later independent change. Withdraw, then preview and restore available recovery. The initial slot remains withdrawn, affected copies cannot return, and unaffected fields recover together.

Sanitize the existing snapshot using the reviewed removal scope. If its remaining state is coherent, retain it with a disclosed reduced scope. If not, discard it and explain that recovery loss before withdrawal confirmation. Apply the boundary whenever snapshots are created, previewed or restored. Initial absence or older source versions in a snapshot must never reopen the withdrawn slot. Clear stale recovery previews after removal. Prefer an explicitly disclosed unavailable snapshot to a misleading partial restoration.

I4 — Separate interruption concealment from handoff.
Origin: Responsible AI interruption requirements incorporated into Design 29 and Map 32. Interaction: cover preserves activity and pending screens but removes working content from visible and accessibility presentation. Underlying controls cannot receive focus; activity-derived announcements stop. Resume returns to a usable control or heading without creating history. Handoff confirmation may be opened from activity or cover; cancellation returns to the preceding screen with work intact.

Human reason: interruptions should not require discarding work. System reason: concealment and reset have different persistence and focus behavior. Acceptance check: cover during an edit, withdrawal review and recovery preview, navigate by keyboard and resume. Confirm handoff from those same states and from practice. No prior marker, draft, dependency, withdrawal boundary, preview or recovery remains available through application controls.

Use genuinely hidden or inert underlying content with a focusable neutral cover screen, rather than a visual overlay alone. Avoid activity-derived accessible labels on cover controls. Handoff must clear the complete state inventory, rendered inputs, summaries, announcements and application-retained references, then construct a fresh empty opening state. Public fictional fixtures may remain. The brief help must say that cover is not a lock and clearing cannot control screenshots, browser history, autofill or device records.

I5 — Render exact sources through one comparison path.
Origin: source and planning requirements in Design 29 and revised Map 32, carrying the Systems engineer's authored fixtures and Learning scientist's descriptive comparison. Interaction: evidence cards, graphics, text equivalents and prepared comparisons derive from fixed public fixture data. Every bar uses a labeled 0–20 cm final-height scale with ticks at 0, 5, 10, 15 and 20. Selection states use words as well as styling.

Human reason: learners should not need visual inference or color recognition to compare records. System reason: separately maintained card, bar and description values can diverge. Acceptance check: inspect every fixture and switch every supported comparison. Values and descriptions must change together; arbitrary wording is displayed literally without execution or automatic judgment. Keep final height distinct from growth and leaves distinct from health.

Source checks: A is water 1 story unit/day, bright light, final height 12 cm, upright leaves. B is water 2, dim light, 18 cm, drooping leaves. C is water 2, bright light, 10 cm, upright leaves. All are an invented 14-day story. Starting height, type and soil remain unrecorded. A/B: B finishes 6 cm taller; water and light differ. A/C: A finishes 2 cm taller; light matches, water differs. B/C: B finishes 8 cm taller; water matches, light differs.

Hold light constant; compare water selects W1/W2: starting height 4 cm, fictional type T, fictional soil mix S, bright light and 14 days match; water is 1/2, final heights are 11/13 cm, and both have upright leaves. W2 finishes 2 cm taller. Hold water constant; compare light selects L1/L2: starting height 4 cm, type T, soil mix S, water 2 and 14 days match; light is bright/dim, final heights are 9/14 cm and leaves upright/drooping. L2 finishes 5 cm taller. These are authored fixtures, not measurements or predictions. Temperature, individual variation, replication and allocation remain unspecified. They do not fill A/B/C gaps or establish causation.

Tradeoffs and alternatives

Selective removal increases complexity and can reduce recovery. A bounded snapshot keeps the promise inspectable, but later actions can replace earlier recovery. Suggested claims lower entry burden while cueing responses. Fixed fixtures expose planning consequences while restricting exploration. Retain the objections that C can feel like a trap, that polished summaries conceal refusal and that withdrawal removes useful history.

Scenario 27 changed the implementation requirement from mandatory retained originals and complete recoverable copies to active retention subject to reviewed withdrawal. Map 32 now closes the withdrawn initial slot and makes recovery subordinate to that boundary. Design 29 must incorporate those details before the candidate is treated as reconciled. This is an existing reconciliation dependency, not a newly observed defect or a request for another Map revision.

The complete teacher-facilitated paper activity is the non-AI alternative and may be preferred. Its distinct paper view must include the mission, exact A/B cards, a separate C reveal sheet, shared-scale graphics and text comparisons, W/L sheets with choice mapping, and before/after records. Include starting claim routes, optional relationships, all reconsideration actions, representation, independent dissent and separate optional practice. Include speech, another language, scribing, passing, correction review and one optional checkpoint. Withdrawal needs reviewed removal of affected lines, copies and checkpoint while preserving independent work; crossing out readable words is not removal. Paper handling and disposal require their own human arrangements.

Acceptance checks

Content and journey checks: exercise every starting claim route without required typing, reveal C, change all three pairs while preserving wording and relationship, switch W/L and return, and complete or skip practice. Inspect equal-status retain/narrow/revise/withhold, literal change feedback, selected but unverified agreement and independent dissent. No outcome may label correctness, causation, proficiency, health or learning.

State and failure checks: use fictional marker strings across active versions, drafts, copied proposals, independent work, previews and recovery. Exercise cancel and confirm from combined states, selective withdrawal, recovery before and after removal, cover/resume and handoff. Try an ordinary edit after withdrawal and verify that it cannot reopen the initial slot. Treat any resurfacing of a reviewed removed marker, silent wording replacement or cross-handoff recovery as a release-blocking technical failure for this candidate.

Access and fallback checks: complete the journey and removal by keyboard; inspect focus order, visible focus, announcements, concealed accessibility content, narrow layout and enlarged text. Inspect user wording containing markup-like characters for literal rendering. Review print styling and whether a teacher can facilitate the entire paper sequence from its materials alone. Human review of reading access, assistive-technology use and workload remains necessary.

Evidence and unknowns

Instrumentation should be limited to a compact, opt-in reviewer panel showing current screen, proposal type, recovery availability, withdrawal-boundary status and invariant failures. It must not duplicate learner wording or retain transition logs, removed content, hidden diagnostic snapshots or participation counts. It creates no telemetry, storage or network traffic. Fictional marker checks are reviewer procedures, not data collection from learners. An invariant display supports diagnosis but does not substitute for interaction and source review.

Useful invariants include a closed initial slot after withdrawal, no blocked dependency in restorable content, no operative retain source after removal, no underlying keyboard access while covered, and unavailable recovery after handoff. A failed invariant should stop the affected commit and preserve current work where possible, with a plain explanation and a route to cancel or facilitate. It must never silently substitute a claim or erase independent work as recovery from an error.

No implementation or checks have been executed in this turn. Intended quality includes inspectable decisions, faithful authorship, agency, dignity, access, belonging and manageable workload. Observed technical behavior is absent; learning, transfer and flourishing evidence remain pending. Unknowns include target devices and browsers, languages, assistance, interruption patterns, feasible lesson time and dependency-review workload. Apparent success could reflect suggestions, adult cues, imitation or fixture familiarity. Difficulty could reflect language access, navigation, group control, time pressure or reasonable rejection of the framing.

Next decision

Reconcile Design 29 with revised Map 32, then have the orchestrator produce one self-contained candidate using these proposed transaction and fixture boundaries. Inspect technical behavior before considering any human pilot. All science-practitioner, teacher, student and caregiver review remains pending. Problem and people

Review receipt for the unchanged source supplied with event 49. Design 29 and revised Map 32 remain the complete provisional brief and capability specification. Middle-school learners investigate fictional garden records with proposed teacher facilitation; no participants or approvals exist. Event 49 reports source recovery after an implementation deadline and an independent syntax-check pass, not completed browser verification.

Human and system capability

Learners retain authority over wording, passing, dissent and withdrawal requests; facilitators must resolve contested attribution and scope. The system supports descriptive comparisons, reviewed records and application-controlled clearing. Controls cannot authenticate authorship, establish agreement or infer learning (Responsible AI 22; Map 32).

Experience and decisions

The source provides a strong mission, A/B comparison, optional initial wording, deliberate C reveal, all three pairs, W/L planning consequences and reviewed before/after positions. At most two main-path wording controls are reused for correction. Optional practice is separate and skippable. Fictional labels and interpretation limits remain beside evidence; help contains review metadata.

Requirements and rationale

Learning scientist 20 requires faithful reconsideration and bounded practice. A blocking source path remains: practiceAction Withhold sets the position to withheld, but a subsequent practiceChoice observation changes only the position. Review and confirmation then permit an observation with action Withhold. This is a source-based finding, not an executed interaction result. Correct the coupled controls so Withhold records no current claim; selecting another position must explicitly resolve the action before confirmation. Preserve cancellation and relationship choices.

Scenario 27 changed mandatory retention into selective withdrawal. Map 32 and Implementation 38 require dependency-aware removal and recovery that cannot resurrect content. The source represents those boundaries through tracked contribution IDs, scope review, sanitization and a closed initial slot. Their actual behavior remains unverified.

Tradeoffs and alternatives

Retain objections about C feeling like a trap, suggestions cueing responses, summaries concealing refusal and withdrawal removing useful history. The supplied standalone paper kit is a complete non-AI route and may be preferred. Facilitation, language support, printing and dependency review impose unknown workload.

Acceptance checks

After correction, exercise observation → Withhold → another observation, and direct position withholding. Review must show one coherent decision; cancel must preserve the committed practice record. Retain must refer to an existing practice position.

Inspect exact fixtures, every pair and W/L switch. Exercise correction, withdrawal cancellation, tracked and additional removal scope, sanitized recovery, cover/resume and confirmed handoff with fictional markers. Check keyboard focus, narrow layout, enlarged text, accessibility concealment and printed paper delivery. None of these checks is claimed performed.

Evidence and unknowns

Event 49 supports only the reported syntax result for the recovered file. Intended quality is inspectable inquiry and faithful representation; browser behavior is unverified. Apparent success could reflect suggestions, imitation or adult cues; difficulty could reflect language, navigation, time or device control. Practitioner, teacher, student and caregiver review, pilots, learning, retention, transfer and flourishing evidence all remain pending.

Next decision

Revisit Build once for the practice-consistency correction, then submit the revised candidate for scoped technical review. Preserve Map 32 and Design 29; no earlier-stage revision is requested. This receipt grants neither field release nor human approval.
